An ideal circuit specifies logical operations. A physical processor must implement them while qubits, gates, measurements, and idle periods can fail. Fault tolerance encodes information across many physical qubits and repeatedly measures error syndromes. These measurements reveal information about errors while preserving the encoded quantum information. The result is a logical operation with a modeled failure probability and a physical space and time cost.

The surface code uses local stabilizer checks on a two-dimensional layout. Its code distance characterizes the smallest undetectable logical error. Increasing distance consumes more physical qubits and more syndrome rounds; the required distance depends on the noise model, decoder, and permitted failure probability. A threshold is a property of those assumptions, rather than a guarantee supplied by the algorithm’s logical qubit count. 

Fowler and colleagues’ surface-code review introduces these constructions and their implementation costs.

Layout matters. Logical data patches, routing space, temporary ancillas, and measurement procedures contribute to the footprint. Operations performed through lattice surgery occupy patches for several syndrome rounds. A logical circuit’s abstract gate depth therefore needs a timing and scheduling model before it becomes elapsed physical time.

Clifford operations preserve stabilizer structure. Universal computation also needs non-Clifford operations, commonly T gates or equivalent injected resources. A factory distills noisy resource states into states suitable for logical computation. Its footprint, throughput, output error, and number of parallel copies must be included in the report. Factories can dominate a small demonstration.

Arbitrary-angle rotations introduce another approximation step: select a synthesis method and allocate precision, then account for the resulting gates or resource states. Counting an undecomposed multi-controlled operation as one physical gate hides substantial work. Likewise, a synthesis cost formula alone does not supply the actual gate sequence or certify its approximation error.

A useful ledger records four different quantities: algorithmic approximation, coherent synthesis approximation, measurement precision and confidence, and physical faults. For one scalar observable, independently justified bias bounds and a statistical interval can be allocated within an absolute error target. A physical fault allowance remains a probability; it is not interchangeable with an observable’s absolute error.

For repeated executions, state whether trials are serial or parallel and allocate failure probability across the complete run. For a hybrid optimizer, include every parameter setting, measurement group, and stopping rule. Confidence for one fixed scalar mean does not establish optimizer convergence or simultaneous confidence for an entire energy sum.

The 

frozen Grover report is a concrete illustration with explicit circuit and hardware assumptions. Other algorithms must supply their own preparation, access, approximation, and output costs. Their reports cannot inherit Grover’s physical counts.

Its arbitrary-rotation reports are conditional resource projections: that helper produces no concrete synthesis sequence or instance-level approximation certificate. The mathematical task is to connect a problem specification to a circuit and a checkable output. This primer collects notation used by the algorithm chapters. It complements the 

quantum-physics primer; no background in formal proof software is required.

A ket |v\rangle is a complex column vector; its bra \langle v| is the conjugate transpose. The inner product and Euclidean norm are\langle v|w\rangle=\sum_j\overline{v_j}w_j,
\qquad \|v\|_2=\sqrt{\langle v|v\rangle}.

Orthogonal vectors have zero inner product. An orthonormal basis gives coordinates without changing lengths. Normalized state vectors have unit norm, while input data vectors may require a separate normalization factor. 

IBM’s inner-products lesson develops these conventions.

Two registers combine by a tensor product: |v\rangle\otimes|w\rangle. Dimensions multiply, so n qubits have 2^n basis states. A joint vector need not factor into individual-register vectors; this is the mathematical possibility behind entanglement. Register order and bit order must match the generator, simulator, and classical comparison. A statevector containing every amplitude therefore has very different storage requirements from a circuit description.

Matrices act linearly on vectors. The adjoint A^\dagger conjugates and transposes; a unitary satisfies U^\dagger U=I and preserves inner products. A Hermitian matrix satisfies H^\dagger=H and has real eigenvalues with an orthonormal eigenbasis:H|u_j\rangle=\lambda_j|u_j\rangle,\qquad
H=\sum_j\lambda_j|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|.

Phase estimation targets the phase in U|u_j\rangle=e^{2\pi i\phi_j}|u_j\rangle. The prepared state’s overlap with the relevant eigenvector affects the chance of obtaining that phase.

Watch Gilbert Strang’s 

MIT 18.06 video, “Lecture 21: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors” for the underlying eigenvector equation. The official lesson includes a video and transcript; quantum phase estimation applies this idea to unitary operators.

A norm makes “close” quantitative. The operator norm\|A\|=\sup_{\|v\|_2=1}\|Av\|_2

measures the largest amplification of a vector. The trace norm \|A\|_1 is the sum of singular values, and the Frobenius norm \|A\|_F=\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}(A^\dagger A)} measures all entries together. These norms give different error guarantees.

For Hermitian H, define f(H) by applying f to its eigenvalues. If a polynomial p approximates f uniformly on an interval containing the spectrum, then\sup_{x\in[a,b]}|p(x)-f(x)|\leq\epsilon
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\|p(H)-f(H)\|\leq\epsilon.

This motivates polynomial methods for evolution and inversion. QSP/QSVT circuits also impose encoding, boundedness, and parity conditions; an arbitrary polynomial fit alone is insufficient. 

PennyLane’s QSVT introduction explains this connection.

Linear-system algorithms must additionally track conditioning. For an invertible matrix, the spectral condition number is \kappa=\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}. Small singular values can make inversion sensitive and expensive. Producing a state proportional to A^{-1}b also leaves its normalization and requested readout to be accounted for. It does not directly return a classical list of every solution component.

For independent preparations with success probability p, R trials all fail with probability (1-p)^R. Repetition costs belong in the algorithm estimate.

For independent Bernoulli outcomes X_1,\ldots,X_M with common mean p, the frequency \hat p=M^{-1}\sum_iX_i estimates that probability. Hoeffding’s bound gives\Pr(|\hat p-p|\geq\epsilon)\leq2e^{-2M\epsilon^2}.

Thus M\geq\ln(2/\delta)/(2\epsilon^2) suffices for confidence at least 1-\delta. 

John Duchi’s Stanford notes state the independence and boundedness assumptions. Sampling confidence controls random variation; it does not remove a biased circuit or an inaccurate model. Specify those errors separately when comparing quantum and classical outputs.

Quantum algorithms use quantum physics to transform information and extract a specified result. This appendix introduces the finite-dimensional language used throughout the handbook. Read it alongside the 

mathematics primer, then follow the quantities you actually need to reproduce an algorithm.

A pure state is a normalized complex vector |\psi\rangle. For one qubit,|\psi\rangle=\alpha|0\rangle+\beta|1\rangle,
\qquad |\alpha|^2+|\beta|^2=1.

Relative phases affect interference. Multiplying the whole vector by the same phase leaves its physical state unchanged. A state describes the system; an observable describes a measurable quantity. Observables are Hermitian operators, such as the Pauli Z operator or the Hamiltonian H, which represents energy.

A density matrix also describes mixtures and subsystems entangled with an environment:\rho=\sum_j p_j|\psi_j\rangle\langle\psi_j|,
\qquad p_j\geq0,\quad \sum_jp_j=1.

It is positive semidefinite and has trace one. Pure states have \rho=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|; different ensembles can describe the same mixed state. Ignoring part of a joint system gives its reduced density matrix by a partial trace. 

IBM’s density-matrix lesson develops this broader description.

For example, |+\rangle=(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt2 and the mixture \rho=I/2 both give equal computational-basis probabilities. They differ when measured in the X basis: the pure state always gives the +1 outcome, whereas the mixture gives either outcome equally often. Matching one measurement distribution therefore does not establish that two states agree.

For an observable A=\sum_a aP_a, a projective measurement returns eigenvalue a with Born-rule probabilityp(a)=\operatorname{Tr}(P_a\rho),
\qquad \langle A\rangle=\operatorname{Tr}(A\rho).

The projectors P_a include any degeneracy. Measuring a pure state in the computational basis gives p(x)=|\langle x|\psi\rangle|^2. One shot produces an outcome; estimating an expectation generally requires repeated preparations and measurements.

For the physical connection between eigenvectors and measurement, watch Barton Zwiebach’s 

MIT 8.04 video, “Completeness of eigenvectors and measurement postulate”. Its official lesson page includes the video and transcript.

Closed-system evolution is unitary:\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^\dagger,\qquad
U(t)=e^{-iHt/\hbar}

for a time-independent Hamiltonian. Circuit gates approximate or compose such transformations; the simulation chapters usually set \hbar=1.

Noise, discarded ancillas, and measurements averaged over their outcomes require quantum channels. A completely positive, trace-preserving map has a Kraus representation\mathcal E(\rho)=\sum_jK_j\rho K_j^\dagger,
\qquad \sum_jK_j^\dagger K_j=I.

Complete positivity ensures valid states even when the input is entangled with another system. Trace preservation retains total probability. A selected measurement branch can instead decrease the trace; that trace records the branch’s success probability. 

IBM’s channel representations explain the channel viewpoint and its implementations.

For a finite-dimensional Hamiltonian, the Gibbs state at inverse temperature \beta=1/(k_BT) is\rho_\beta=\frac{e^{-\beta H}}{Z(\beta)},
\qquad Z(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H}).

The partition function normalizes the state; exponentiating a Hamiltonian alone does not produce a normalized density matrix. Energy eigenstates receive weights proportional to e^{-\beta E_j}. See David Tong’s 

statistical-physics notes on the canonical ensemble.

Choose an output metric before estimating resources. A search task needs a correct answer with stated probability. An energy task needs observable accuracy and sampling confidence. A state-preparation task may use trace distance D(\rho,\sigma)=\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1, which bounds changes in measurement-event probabilities. Fidelity measures similarity; specify whether it is squared or unsquared, as 

IBM’s fidelity lesson emphasizes. The 

resource baseline accounts separately for algorithmic approximation, sampling requirements, and physical faults.

def explore_amplitude(n_data, threshold, phase_bits):
    if not 1 <= n_data <= 3 or not 2 <= phase_bits <= 4:
        raise ValueError("Live controls are capped at 3 data bits and 4 phase bits")
    if not 0 <= threshold <= 2**n_data:
        raise ValueError("Threshold is outside the selected register")
    law = simulate_amplitude_estimation(n_data, threshold, phase_bits)
    reference = analytic_amplitude_distribution(threshold/2**n_data, phase_bits)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(law, reference, atol=2e-12, rtol=0)
    print({"exact_probability": threshold/2**n_data,
           "live_qubits": n_data+1+phase_bits,
           "controlled_Q_calls": 2**phase_bits-1,
           "max_analytic_error": float(np.max(np.abs(law-reference)))})
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 2.8))
    ax.bar(range(2**phase_bits), law, color="#18786e")
    ax.set(xlabel="Phase outcome", ylabel="Ideal probability")
    plt.show()

A classical controller selects an amplification power from its existing confidence interval. Every new round samples a fresh fixed-size batch from an explicit A; Q^power; flag measurement circuit. There is no phase register or controlled-Q. This bounded variant specifies its own confidence allocation/caps; it does not automatically inherit the original IQAE complexity constants. The threshold probability is known and supplies an independent check, not an advantage benchmark.

With T declared in advance, each new fixed-N binomial interval gets delta/T. Conditional coverage and a union bound give P(conclusive and wrong) <= delta under the exact ideal law. This does not imply P(correct | conclusive) >= 1-delta. A cap can remain inconclusive; The core checks exact rational binomial-tail inequalities, monotone branch conditions, outward trigonometric enclosures and the returned radius. These executed arithmetic certificates are separate from any formal proof of the PRNG or hardware law. The seed and full status remain part of the result.

from pathlib import Path
import hashlib, importlib.util, json, os, stat, sys

def read_regular(path, cap):
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    try:
        before = os.fstat(fd)
        assert stat.S_ISREG(before.st_mode) and 0 <= before.st_size <= cap
        with os.fdopen(fd, 'rb', closefd=False) as handle:
            raw = handle.read(cap + 1)
        after = os.fstat(fd)
        named = os.stat(path, follow_symlinks=False)
        identity = lambda info: (info.st_dev, info.st_ino, info.st_size, info.st_mtime_ns, info.st_ctime_ns)
        assert len(raw) == before.st_size and identity(before) == identity(after) == identity(named)
        return raw
    finally:
        os.close(fd)

A supplied coherent preparation A and good-register predicate are required. The schedule uses a lower bound w, without reading the exact initial success probability. The guarantee is ideal failure probability at most δ² for p≥w. Floating phases, numerical checks and conditional surface-code projections are distinct evidence.

The threshold preparation below has a trivial classical answer. It demonstrates explicit preparation, inverse and phased reflections; it is not an application speedup.

A applies Hadamards to the data and computes the reversible threshold flag. Each round applies good phase β, A†, all-zero phase −α, A and global π. The zero projector covers the complete data-plus-flag register. No dense unitary or initialized state replaces preparation or inversion.

display(A.draw(output="mpl",style="iqp"))
plt.close("all")

plt.close("all")

The success law is 1−δ² T_L(√(1−p)/γ)², with γ=sech(acosh(1/δ)/L). A long-double polynomial recurrence independently checks the production trigonometric formula. Direct source/target projector matrices independently check the full operator, including global phase.

def recurrence_success(p,L,delta):
    if p in (0.,1.):return p
    gamma=np.longdouble(1)/np.cosh(np.arccosh(np.longdouble(1)/delta)/L)
    x=np.sqrt(np.longdouble(1)-p)/gamma
    previous,current=np.longdouble(1),x
    for _ in range(2,L+1):previous,current=current,2*x*current-previous
    return float(1-(np.longdouble(delta)*current)**2)
p=threshold/2**n_data

expected=recurrence_success(p,schedule.length,delta)
assert abs(actual-expected)<2e-12
assert abs(ideal_success_probability(p,schedule)-expected)<2e-12
a=Operator(A).data
psi=a[:,0]
identity=np.eye(len(psi),dtype=complex)
good=np.diag([int((i>>n_data)&1) for i in range(len(psi))])
reference=a.copy()
for alpha,beta in zip(schedule.alphas,schedule.betas,strict=True):
    reference=-(identity+(np.exp(-1j*alpha)-1)*np.outer(psi,psi.conj())) @ (identity+(np.exp(1j*beta)-1)*good) @ reference
operator_error=float(np.max(np.abs(Operator(circuit).data-reference)))
state_error=float(np.max(np.abs(Statevector.from_instruction(circuit).data-
                               Statevector.from_instruction(compiled.remove_final_measurements(inplace=False)).data)))
assert operator_error<2e-12 and state_error<2e-12

       "full_operator_max_error":operator_error,"lowered_state_max_error":state_error})

ax.axhline(1-delta**2,ls="--",color="#29485b",label="Ideal promised success bound")
ax.axvline(lower,ls=":",color="#29485b")
ax.set(xlabel="Initial preparation success p",ylabel="Ideal output success",ylim=(-.025,1.025),xlim=(0,1))

import os
import numpy as np


def simulate_interactive_case(n_qubits, marked, iterations):
    """Bounded ideal simulation shared by the controls and deterministic checks."""
    if not 2 <= n_qubits <= 6:
        raise ValueError("Live controls support 2–6 qubits")
    if not 0 <= iterations <= 12:
        raise ValueError("Live controls support 0–12 iterations")
    marked = min(max(int(marked), 0), 2**n_qubits - 1)
    circuit = build_grover_circuit(n_qubits, marked, iterations)
    probabilities = Statevector.from_instruction(circuit).probabilities()
    expected = expected_success_probability(n_qubits, iterations)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(probabilities[marked], expected, atol=1e-10, rtol=0)
    return circuit, probabilities, marked, expected


for validation_n in range(2, 7):
    for validation_marked in (0, 2**validation_n - 1):
        for validation_iterations in (0, optimal_iterations(validation_n), 12):
            simulate_interactive_case(validation_n, validation_marked, validation_iterations)
print("Validated 30 bounded cases; every live evaluation also checks the analytic probability.")

# Binder and local kernels display live controls when this cell is run.
if os.environ.get("OPENQUANTUM_STATIC_BUILD") == "1":
    print("Live Python controls are available when this notebook is run in Binder or JupyterLab.")
else:
    import ipywidgets as widgets

    n_control = widgets.IntSlider(value=3, min=2, max=6, description="Qubits", continuous_update=False)
    marked_control = widgets.IntSlider(value=5, min=0, max=7, description="Marked", continuous_update=False)
    iterations_control = widgets.IntSlider(value=2, min=0, max=12, description="Iterations", continuous_update=False)

    def update_marked_range(change):
        marked_control.max = 2**change["new"] - 1

    n_control.observe(update_marked_range, names="value")

    def render_live_case(n_qubits, marked, iterations):

        target = f"{marked:0{n_qubits}b}"

        "n_qubits": n_control, "marked": marked_control, "iterations": iterations_control
    })

Positive k means variable k-1; negative k means its negation. The assignment occupies the low-index data qubits and clause scratch starts in zero. The oracle computes clauses, marks their conjunction by phase, and uncomputes every clause.

def independent_cnf_value(formula, assignment):
    def literal_value(literal):
        bit = bool((assignment >> (abs(literal) - 1)) & 1)
        return bit if literal > 0 else not bit
    return all(any(literal_value(literal) for literal in clause) for clause in formula.clauses)

n = cnf.n_variables
dimension = 2 ** oracle.num_qubits
for assignment in range(2**n):
    after = Statevector.from_int(assignment, dims=dimension).evolve(oracle)
    expected = np.zeros(dimension, dtype=complex)
    expected[assignment] = -1 if independent_cnf_value(cnf, assignment) else 1
    np.testing.assert_allclose(after.data, expected, atol=1e-10, rtol=0)

uniform = np.zeros(dimension, dtype=complex)
uniform[:2**n] = 1 / np.sqrt(2**n)
after = Statevector(uniform).evolve(oracle)
signed = uniform.copy()
for assignment in range(2**n):
    if independent_cnf_value(cnf, assignment):
        signed[assignment] *= -1
np.testing.assert_allclose(after.data, signed, atol=1e-10, rtol=0)

Let W include the actual preparation and LCU, S_g=I-2\Pi_{\rm labels=0}, and S_0=I-2|0\cdots0\rangle\langle0\cdots0| on every initial wire. One Grover round after W is chronological S_g,W^\dagger,S_0,W, plus a global minus sign.

The full initial-state reflection makes this ordinary known-input amplitude amplification. It does not attempt oblivious amplification of an unknown nonunitary inverse. Its successful state direction is unchanged in the ideal model. Integer-round success is nonmonotone, so more rounds need not improve it.

diagram.append(initial.to_gate(label='S0: all wires zero'), range(source.num_qubits))

An odd polynomial approximates a scaled inverse across a promised signed Hermitian spectrum. The input is an explicit Pauli matrix and a reproducible gate-built complex vector. Matrix-access PREPARE/SELECT/unprepare and projector phases are actual gates. Dense spectral analysis and a classical solve appear only as independent small-instance references.

This notebook reuses original MIT implementation code and records exact rational polynomial facts separately from phase, access and synthesis errors. It uses the pinned Qiskit/NumPy/SciPy environment. Saved outputs can be published statically; optional live controls require a Python kernel.

from pathlib import Path
from fractions import Fraction
import sys, os, json
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import display
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
root = Path.cwd()
if not (root/'src/openquantum/linear_systems_qsvt_reciprocal.py').exists() and (root.parent/'src/openquantum/linear_systems_qsvt_reciprocal.py').exists():
    root = root.parent

elif (root/'code/src/openquantum/linear_systems_qsvt_reciprocal.py').exists():
    sys.path.insert(0, str(root/'code/src'))
from openquantum import linear_systems_qsvt_reciprocal as inv
from openquantum.reciprocal_phase_certificate import certify_real_qsp_phases
terms = inv.DEFAULT_TERMS
K = inv.choose_k('1/2', '.01')
model = inv.ReciprocalPolynomial(K, Fraction(1,2))
prep = inv.default_preparation(2)
print('Explicit input:', terms)
print('K, odd degree, scale:', K, model.degree, model.scale)
print('Promised signed interval: 1/2 <= |lambda(A/alpha)| <= 1')

With m=K+1 and c=1/\lceil\sqrt m\rceil,p_K(x)=c\,x\sum_{j=0}^{K}(1-x^2)^j.

It is odd and bounded by one across [-1,1]. On a promised spectrum \delta\le|x|\le1, relative inverse error is at most E=(1-\delta^2)^m. The positive relative factor has eigenvalues in [1-E,1], giving normalized-state trace distance E/(2-E) and Pauli-mean bias 2E/(2-E).

The degree is O(\delta^{-2}\log(1/\epsilon_A)) for a Pauli-bias target \epsilon_A. This original geometric polynomial does not achieve the optimal condition dependence of more advanced QSVT reciprocal approximations.

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.7,3.4))
for interval in ((-1.,-.5),(.5,1.)):
    grid = np.linspace(*interval,401)

            label='Requested scaled reciprocal' if interval[0]>0 else None)
    ax.plot(grid, inv.reciprocal_polynomial(grid,K), color='#216e90',
            label=f'Geometric polynomial, degree {model.degree}' if interval[0]>0 else None)
ax.axvspan(-.5,.5,alpha=.1,color='gray',label='Excluded spectral gap')
ax.set(xlabel='Normalized signed eigenvalue',ylabel='Accepted filter amplitude')
ax.grid(alpha=.2); ax.legend(fontsize=8); plt.show()
display(pd.DataFrame([{
    'degree': model.degree,
    'relative tail bound': float(model.relative_tail),
    'scaled operator error bound': model.as_metadata()['scaled_inverse_operator_error_bound'],
    'conditional trace bound': float(model.trace_bound),
    'conditional Pauli bias bound': float(model.pauli_bias_bound),
    'target acceptance lower bound': float(model.success_lower_bound)
}]))

A readable coarse demonstration uses one data qubit, A=3I-X, normalization four and promised gap one-half. Setting K=1 gives degree three. The circuit below contains the actual positive-amplitude loading, signed Pauli SELECT, unprepare, real-part flag and all final measurements. This is a lower-accuracy demonstration; the default degree33 circuit is checked separately.

The degree33 source contains 33 complete matrix-access calls and 34 projector phases. The compact gate below has those actual definitions; the exported measured QASM contains primitive operations.

All data, label and flag bits are measured. Acceptance checks only zero labels and zero flag. Final X readout adds H; Y readout adds S-dagger then H. Every failed attempt incurs the complete preparation/access/readout schedule.

It reproduces exact-statevector optimization, then performs a separate finite-shot experiment at parameters selected by the first prescribed initialization. Save the public optimization.py download beside this notebook to run it independently, or run from the source checkout. Use the published Python 3.12 environment lock. No live widgets or public kernel service are required to serve the saved outputs. The original QAOA algorithm is due to Farhi, Goldstone and Gutmann (2014), arXiv:1411.4028 Farhi et al., 2014; the original VQE demonstration is due to Peruzzo et al. (2014), DOI:10.1038/ncomms5213 Peruzzo et al., 2014. The chapter bibliography provides full citations and the exact Qiskit and NumPy releases Qiskit contributors, n.d. NumPy Developers, n.d.. records.content:
The MaxCut graph is the cycle with vertices 0,1,2,3 and edges (0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(0,3). The objective is the number of cut edges,C(z)=\sum_{(u,v)}\frac{1-Z_uZ_v}{2}.

Qiskit wire q[0] is the least significant bit. Displayed bitstrings read q[3] q[2] q[1] q[0]. We enumerate all 16 assignments before using a quantum circuit.

For VQE the input is the explicit HamiltonianH=-Z_0-Z_1+\tfrac12X_0X_1.

The independent NumPy matrix uses basis order |00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle. Exact diagonalization is a reference calculation on this four-dimensional input.

edges = tuple(opt.CYCLE_EDGES)
n_qubits = 4
cut_values = np.array([
    sum(((assignment >> u) & 1) != ((assignment >> v) & 1) for u, v in edges)
    for assignment in range(2**n_qubits)
], dtype=float)
np.testing.assert_array_equal(opt.maxcut_values(n_qubits, edges), cut_values)
classical_cut_optimum = float(cut_values.max())
classical_best_strings = [f"{i:04b}" for i in np.flatnonzero(cut_values == classical_cut_optimum)]

I = np.eye(2)
X = np.array([[0., 1.], [1., 0.]])
Z = np.diag([1., -1.])
independent_hamiltonian = -np.kron(I, Z) - np.kron(Z, I) + .5*np.kron(X, X)
np.testing.assert_allclose(opt.vqe_hamiltonian(), independent_hamiltonian, atol=1e-14, rtol=0)
exact_eigenvalues = np.linalg.eigvalsh(independent_hamiltonian)
exact_ground_energy = float(exact_eigenvalues[0])
np.testing.assert_allclose(exact_ground_energy, -np.sqrt(4.25), atol=1e-14, rtol=0)
print({"MaxCut optimum": classical_cut_optimum, "optimal bitstrings": classical_best_strings,
       "Hamiltonian eigenvalues": exact_eigenvalues.tolist()})

records.content:
Depth-one QAOA prepares |+\rangle^{\otimes4}, applies e^{-i\gamma C}, then e^{-i\beta\sum_jX_j}. Each cost edge is implemented by CX; RZ(-gamma); CX; its omitted global phase does not affect the output. The mixer uses RX(2 beta). The minimizer receives -\langle C\rangle.

The VQE circuit prepares R_Y(\theta) on qubit 0 and then CX(0,1). It has state \cos(\theta/2)|00\rangle+\sin(\theta/2)|11\rangle and minimizes \langle H\rangle.

Every objective evaluation below checks the independently derived formulas\langle C\rangle=2+\sin(4\beta)\sin(2\gamma),\qquad
E(\theta)=-2\cos\theta+\tfrac12\sin\theta.

The deterministic coordinate polling optimizer starts with step 0.4 radians, evaluates both directions of each coordinate in a fixed order, accepts an improvement greater than 

10-12, and halves its step when no candidate improves the current value. It stops when the step is below 

10-6 radians or after 128 iterations. Angles are periodic modulo 2\pi. These stopping rules are empirical search settings, not a bound on the objective gap.

All three initializations are fixed below. The first run is selected for plots and sampled readout in advance. The complete canonical traces, including every trial objective and measured optimizer time, are in the downloadable runs.json and evaluations.csv. This notebook executes new reproductions; its measured times can differ from those artifacts.

def checked_qaoa_objective(parameters):
    gamma, beta = parameters
    observed = opt.qaoa_expectation(n_qubits, edges, [gamma], [beta])
    predicted = 2 + np.sin(4*beta)*np.sin(2*gamma)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(observed, predicted, atol=2e-12, rtol=0)
    return -observed


def checked_vqe_objective(parameters):
    theta = parameters[0]
    observed = opt.vqe_expectation(theta)
    predicted = -2*np.cos(theta) + .5*np.sin(theta)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(observed, predicted, atol=2e-12, rtol=0)
    return observed


search_settings = dict(initial_step=.4, step_tolerance=1e-6,
                       improvement_tolerance=1e-12, max_iterations=128)
qaoa_initializations = [(0.2, 0.1), (0.6, 0.4), (-0.3, 0.25)]
vqe_initializations = [(0.6,), (-1.1,), (2.2,)]
qaoa_runs, vqe_runs = [], []
reproduction_seconds = {"qaoa": [], "vqe": []}
for name, objective, starts, destination in (
    ("qaoa", checked_qaoa_objective, qaoa_initializations, qaoa_runs),
    ("vqe", checked_vqe_objective, vqe_initializations, vqe_runs),
):
    for initial in starts:
        started = perf_counter()
        result = opt.pattern_search(objective, initial, objective_method="exact_statevector", **search_settings)
        reproduction_seconds[name].append(perf_counter() - started)
        destination.append(result)

qaoa_result, vqe_result = qaoa_runs[0], vqe_runs[0]
gamma, beta = qaoa_result["parameters"]
theta = vqe_result["parameters"][0]
qaoa_expected_cut = -qaoa_result["value"]
vqe_energy = vqe_result["value"]
assert abs(qaoa_expected_cut - 3) < 1e-8
assert abs(vqe_energy - exact_ground_energy) < 1e-8
print("All objective evaluations passed their independent analytic checks.")



rows = ["| Workflow / fixed start | Final exact objective | Evaluations | Iterations | Stop | Reproduction seconds |",
        "|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|"]
for name, starts, runs in (("QAOA expected cut", qaoa_initializations, qaoa_runs),
                          ("VQE energy", vqe_initializations, vqe_runs)):
    for index, (initial, result) in enumerate(zip(starts, runs)):
        objective = -result["value"] if name.startswith("QAOA") else result["value"]
        seconds = reproduction_seconds["qaoa" if name.startswith("QAOA") else "vqe"][index]
        rows.append(f"| {name}, {initial} | {objective:.10f} | {len(result['evaluations'])} | "
                    f"{len(result['iterations'])} | {result['stop_reason']} | {seconds:.4f} |")
rows += ["", f"The classical cut optimum is {classical_cut_optimum:g}; the first QAOA run's exact expected-cut ratio is "
         f"{qaoa_expected_cut/classical_cut_optimum:.10f}. The first VQE run's gap to the exact ground energy is "
         f"{vqe_energy-exact_ground_energy:.3g}. These are exact-statevector results on the specified small inputs."]
display_result_table(rows)



figure, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.5))
colors = ["#246b72", "#a2573c", "#7a6a9b"]
for run, color, initial in zip(qaoa_runs, colors, qaoa_initializations):
    values = np.array([entry["value"] for entry in run["evaluations"]])
    axes[0].plot(np.arange(1, len(values)+1), -np.minimum.accumulate(values),
                 color=color, label=str(initial))
axes[0].axhline(3, color="#555555", ls="--", lw=1, label="depth-one optimum")
axes[0].set(xlabel="Objective evaluations", ylabel="Best exact expected cut",
            title="QAOA: prescribed initializations")
axes[0].legend(fontsize=8)
for run, color, initial in zip(vqe_runs, colors, vqe_initializations):
    values = np.array([entry["value"] for entry in run["evaluations"]])
    gaps = np.maximum(np.minimum.accumulate(values)-exact_ground_energy, 1e-14)
    axes[1].semilogy(np.arange(1, len(values)+1), gaps, color=color, label=str(initial))
axes[1].set(xlabel="Objective evaluations", ylabel="Best exact energy gap",
            title="VQE: prescribed initializations")
axes[1].legend(fontsize=8)
figure.tight_layout()
plt.show()
plt.close(figure)

Optimization above uses zero shots: each objective is evaluated by an ideal statevector. The following held-out sampling experiments evaluate the first optimized parameters with seeds 7, 19 and 41. They do not train a noisy or sampled optimizer.

For QAOA, a single all-Z measurement of all four qubits supplies every edge contribution and a candidate cut. Each seeded experiment uses 2,048 independently simulated shots.

For VQE, measure both qubits in Z to estimate the joint observable -Z_0-Z_1, preserving the covariance of its terms. In a separate group, apply H to both qubits and measure Z to estimate \tfrac12X_0X_1. Each group uses 2,048 shots per seed. Group sample means are added, and their sample variances determine a descriptive estimated standard error. This standard error is not a confidence or device-error guarantee.

Sampling uses the implementation’s NumPy Generator(PCG64) multinomial sampler from the actual circuit probabilities. The QAOA and VQE Z groups use the listed seed; the independent VQE X stream uses that seed plus 1,000,003. The notebook recomputes every sampled mean and group standard error directly from the returned counts. State preparation and the change of measurement basis are present in the generated circuits. Device noise, mitigation, fault-tolerant synthesis and hardware execution time are excluded.

shots_per_group = 2048
sampling_seeds = (7, 19, 41)
z_group_probabilities = Statevector.from_instruction(opt.build_vqe_circuit(theta, basis="z")).probabilities()
x_group_probabilities = Statevector.from_instruction(opt.build_vqe_circuit(theta, basis="x")).probabilities()
indices_two = np.arange(4)
z0 = 1-2*(indices_two & 1)
z1 = 1-2*((indices_two >> 1) & 1)
z_group_values = -z0-z1
x_group_values = .5*z0*z1
np.testing.assert_allclose(np.dot(z_group_probabilities, z_group_values)
                           + np.dot(x_group_probabilities, x_group_values),
                           vqe_energy, atol=1e-12, rtol=0)


def observed_mean_and_standard_error(counts_by_bitstring, values):
    counts = np.array([counts_by_bitstring.get(f"{index:0{int(np.log2(len(values)))}b}", 0)
                       for index in range(len(values))])
    count = int(np.sum(counts))
    mean = float(np.dot(counts, values)/count)
    variance = float(np.dot(counts, (values-mean)**2)/(count-1))
    return mean, np.sqrt(variance/count)


sample_records = []
for seed in sampling_seeds:
    q_readout = opt.sample_qaoa(gamma, beta, shots=shots_per_group, seed=seed)
    v_readout = opt.sample_vqe(theta, shots=shots_per_group, seed=seed)
    q_mean, q_se = observed_mean_and_standard_error(q_readout["counts"], cut_values)
    z_group, x_group = v_readout["groups"]
    z_mean, z_se = observed_mean_and_standard_error(z_group["counts"], z_group_values)
    x_mean, x_se = observed_mean_and_standard_error(x_group["counts"], x_group_values)
    np.testing.assert_allclose([q_mean, q_se],
                               [q_readout["estimate"], q_readout["estimated_standard_error"]],
                               atol=1e-12, rtol=0)
    np.testing.assert_allclose([z_mean+x_mean, np.hypot(z_se, x_se)],
                               [v_readout["estimate"], v_readout["estimated_standard_error"]],
                               atol=1e-12, rtol=0)
    assert sum(q_readout["counts"].values()) == shots_per_group
    assert sum(z_group["counts"].values()) == shots_per_group
    assert sum(x_group["counts"].values()) == shots_per_group
    sample_records.append({"seed": seed, "qaoa": q_readout, "vqe": v_readout})
rows = ["| Seed | Sampled mean cut | Cut SE | Optimal-cut fraction | Sampled VQE energy | Energy SE |",
        "|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|"]
for record in sample_records:
    q, v = record["qaoa"], record["vqe"]
    rows.append(f"| {record['seed']} | {q['estimate']:.6f} | {q['estimated_standard_error']:.6f} | "
                f"{q['optimal_cut_sample_fraction']:.6f} | {v['estimate']:.6f} | {v['estimated_standard_error']:.6f} |")
display_result_table(rows)
print({"exact-optimization shots": 0, "sampled QAOA shots across three seeds": 3*shots_per_group,
       "sampled VQE shots across three seeds and two groups": 3*2*shots_per_group,
       "combined sampled shots": 3*3*shots_per_group})

records.content:
For the unweighted cycle \mathcal E=\{(0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(0,3)\}, defineC(z)=\sum_{(u,v)\in\mathcal E}[z_u\ne z_v],\qquad
H_D=-\sum_{q=0}^{3}X_q,\qquad
H_P=\frac12\sum_{(u,v)\in\mathcal E}Z_uZ_v=2I-C.

The time-dependent Hamiltonian is H(s)=(1-s)H_D+sH_P, with linear s=t/T and \hbar=1. Energy and time are in the associated dimensionless units. Initial H gates prepare |+\rangle^{\otimes4}, the driver ground state. The two optimal cut strings 0101 and 1010 are a degenerate final ground space; success means total probability in that space.

For \Delta t=T/L and midpoint s_j=(j+1/2)/L, each step applies a driver half-step, a problem full-step, and another driver half-step. With R_P(\alpha)=e^{-i\alpha P/2}, the chronological primitive gates are:

rx(-dt*(1-s_j)) on every qubit;

cx(u,v); rz(dt*s_j,v); cx(u,v) for every edge;

the same RX half-step on every qubit.

The signs follow H_D=-\sum X: each driver half-step is \exp(+i\Delta t(1-s_j)\sum X/2). The ZZ phase realizes \exp(-i\Delta t s_j\sum ZZ/2). No opaque Hamiltonian evolution operation is hidden in the generated circuit.

edges = ((0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3), (0, 3))
n_qubits = 4
basis_indices = np.arange(1 << n_qubits)
cut_values = np.array([sum(((z >> u) & 1) != ((z >> v) & 1) for u, v in edges)
                       for z in basis_indices], dtype=float)
np.testing.assert_array_equal(cut_values, opt.maxcut_values(n_qubits, edges))
optimal_mask = cut_values == cut_values.max()
assert cut_values.max() == 4
initial_state = np.ones(16, dtype=complex)/4
# Bit flips construct independent matrices in |q3 q2 q1 q0> order.
driver = -sum(np.eye(16, dtype=complex)[:, basis_indices ^ (1 << q)] for q in range(4))
zz_energies = np.array([.5*sum((1-2*((z >> u)&1))*(1-2*((z >> v)&1)) for u,v in edges)
                        for z in basis_indices])
np.testing.assert_array_equal(zz_energies, 2-cut_values)
problem = np.diag(zz_energies)
np.testing.assert_allclose(driver @ initial_state, -4*initial_state, atol=1e-14, rtol=0)
print({"classical_maximum_cut": float(cut_values.max()),
       "optimal_bitstrings": [f"{z:04b}" for z in basis_indices[optimal_mask]],
       "initial_driver_energy": float(np.vdot(initial_state, driver @ initial_state).real)})


def dense_strang(total_time, steps):
    # Classical 16d reference assembled independently of the circuit API.
    dt = total_time/steps
    eigenvalues, eigenvectors = np.linalg.eigh(driver)
    state = initial_state.copy()
    for j in range(steps):
        s = (j+.5)/steps
        half = (eigenvectors*np.exp(-1j*dt*(1-s)*eigenvalues/2)) @ eigenvectors.conj().T
        state = half @ state
        state *= np.exp(-1j*dt*s*zz_energies)
        state = half @ state
    return state


def continuous_reference(total_time):
    # Independent dense numerical solution of i d|psi>/dt=H(t/T)|psi>.
    solution = solve_ivp(lambda t, y: -1j*((1-t/total_time)*driver+(t/total_time)*problem) @ y,
                         (0, total_time), initial_state, method="DOP853", rtol=1e-11, atol=1e-13)
    assert solution.success, solution.message
    return solution.y[:, -1], {"method": "SciPy DOP853", "rtol": 1e-11, "atol": 1e-13,
                              "function_evaluations": solution.nfev,
                              "norm_drift": float(abs(np.vdot(solution.y[:, -1], solution.y[:, -1]).real-1))}


def state_observables(state):
    probabilities = np.abs(state)**2/np.vdot(state,state).real
    return {"expected_cut": float(probabilities @ cut_values),
            "optimal_cut_probability": float(probabilities[optimal_mask].sum())}


def comparison(state, reference):
    fidelity = abs(np.vdot(state, reference))**2/(np.vdot(state,state).real*np.vdot(reference,reference).real)
    return {"state_infidelity": float(max(0., 1-fidelity)),
            "absolute_cut_mean_error": abs(state_observables(state)["expected_cut"]-state_observables(reference)["expected_cut"])}



def independent_gate_circuit(total_time, steps, measure=False):
    # A separate explicit construction for differential checking on four qubits.
    if not 0 < total_time <= 16 or not isinstance(steps, int) or not 1 <= steps <= 256:
        raise ValueError("this notebook's independent checker is bounded to T<=16 and 1..256 steps")
    dt = total_time/steps
    circuit = QuantumCircuit(4)
    circuit.h(range(4))
    for j in range(steps):
        s = (j+.5)/steps
        circuit.rx(-dt*(1-s), range(4))
        for u,v in edges:
            circuit.cx(u,v)
            circuit.rz(dt*s,v)
            circuit.cx(u,v)
        circuit.rx(-dt*(1-s), range(4))
    if measure:
        circuit.measure_all()
    return circuit

The full spectral gap E_1-E_0 reaches zero at s=1, because the two maximum-cut basis states are degenerate. The ideal Hamiltonians commute with the global bit flip G=X^{\otimes4}, and the initial state is in its G=+1 sector. We therefore also inspect the first gap within that sector.

The sector calculation is an eight-dimensional classical eigensolver reduction. The physical circuit still has four logical qubits. Positivity on a 201-point mesh is a numerical observation, not a proven lower bound between mesh points, an adiabatic theorem, a general runtime guarantee, or a promise that hardware noise preserves this symmetry.

np.testing.assert_allclose(driver@global_flip, global_flip@driver, rtol=0, atol=1e-14)
np.testing.assert_allclose(problem@global_flip, global_flip@problem, rtol=0, atol=1e-14)
np.testing.assert_allclose(global_flip@initial_state, initial_state, rtol=0, atol=1e-14)
np.testing.assert_allclose(global_flip@main_state, main_state, rtol=0, atol=1e-10)
plus_basis = np.column_stack([(np.eye(16)[:, z]+np.eye(16)[:, z ^ 15])/np.sqrt(2) for z in range(8)])
np.testing.assert_allclose(plus_basis.T@plus_basis, np.eye(8), rtol=0, atol=1e-14)
np.testing.assert_allclose(global_flip@plus_basis, plus_basis, rtol=0, atol=1e-14)
mesh = np.linspace(0,1,201)

for s in mesh:
    hamiltonian = (1-s)*driver+s*problem

The notebook performs saved-record checks only: it does not optimize angles, draw new samples, synthesize rotations or query a physical estimator. Actual Clifford+T sequences, logical line routing, explicit input resets, all repeated preparations and joint all-Z readout must be inspectable in the saved circuit bundle.

The conditional surface-code scenario includes specified initialization, readout, routing/injection, feedback and capped factory-supply assumptions. Numerical synthesis guards and tiny ideal checks are evidence rather than formal interval certificates or hardware calibration. No convergence, unchanged adaptive-path, quantum-advantage or hardware-success guarantee follows. Classical C4 reference coverage only. The earlier VQE ideal hits keep their original inconclusive holdout labels.

The saved original physical attempt failed at the representation boundary. One declared computation-only recovery preserved all 54 synthesized checkpoints and used a lossless shared JSON-DAG representation. Both native-query counts and CPU times remain charged; source preparations and T states are counted once. Complete first-pass point records were unavailable, so no equality to that missing result is claimed. This public audit requires no private pickle.

records.content:
The original sampler scored all cut edges jointly. Recomputing the mean and sample variance from each integer bitstring count retains within-shot covariance. The decision replay uses those sampled values and errors, not an exact expectation. All proposals follow the fixed coordinate order and periodic angle domain; equality with the descriptive margin is rejected.

WIDTH = 4
EDGES = ((0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3), (0, 3))
INDICES = np.arange(1 << WIDTH)
CUTS = np.array([sum(((z >> u) ^ (z >> v)) & 1 for u, v in EDGES)
                 for z in INDICES], dtype=float)
assert int(CUTS.max()) == 4

def count_moments(group):
    shots, counts = group['shots'], group['counts']
    assert isinstance(shots, int) and not isinstance(shots, bool) and shots >= 2
    assert counts and sum(counts.values()) == shots
    assert all(isinstance(number, int) and not isinstance(number, bool) and number > 0
               and len(bits) == WIDTH and not (set(bits) - {'0', '1'})
               for bits, number in counts.items())
    mean = sum(number * CUTS[int(bits, 2)] for bits, number in counts.items()) / shots
    variance = sum(number * (CUTS[int(bits, 2)] - mean) ** 2
                   for bits, number in counts.items()) / (shots - 1)
    return mean, variance, math.sqrt(variance / shots)

def wrap(point):
    return (np.asarray(point, dtype=float) + np.pi) % (2 * np.pi) - np.pi

def replay_count_decisions(run):
    assert run['initial'] == [.6, .4, .6, .4]
    assert run['seed'] == 7 and run['stream_id'] == 33
    assert run['objective_evaluations'] == len(run['evaluations']) == 109
    assert len(run['iterations']) == 12 and run['convergence_certified'] is False
    point, current = wrap(run['initial']), run['evaluations'][0]
    calls, accepted_indexes, index = run['evaluations'], set(), 1
    allocations = [128] + [shots for shots in (260, 520, 1040) for _ in range(36)]
    assert [call['index'] for call in calls] == list(range(109))
    for call, shots in zip(calls, allocations):
        assert [group['group'] for group in call['groups']] == ['all_z']
        assert call['total_shots'] == shots == call['groups'][0]['shots']
        mean, variance, se = count_moments(call['groups'][0])
        np.testing.assert_allclose([call['objective_estimate'], call['estimated_standard_error'],
                                   call['groups'][0]['estimate'], call['groups'][0]['sample_variance']],
                                  [-mean, se, mean, variance], rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12)
    assert current['role'] == 'initial' and not current['accepted']
    np.testing.assert_allclose(current['parameters'], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-14)
    for sweep, iteration in enumerate(run['iterations']):
        incumbent = calls[index]
        proposal_indexes = list(range(index + 1, index + 9))
        assert iteration['index'] == sweep
        assert iteration['step'] == (.4, .2, .1)[sweep // 4]
        assert iteration['shots_per_group'] == (260, 520, 1040)[sweep // 4]
        assert iteration['incumbent_evaluation'] == index
        assert iteration['proposal_evaluations'] == proposal_indexes
        assert incumbent['role'] == 'incumbent' and not incumbent['accepted']
        np.testing.assert_allclose(incumbent['parameters'], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-14)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(iteration['parameters_before'], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-14)
        proposals = [calls[number] for number in proposal_indexes]
        for offset, proposal in enumerate(proposals):
            axis, direction = offset // 2, -1 if offset % 2 == 0 else 1
            assert proposal['role'] == 'proposal'
            assert (proposal['axis'], proposal['direction']) == (axis, direction)
            trial = point.copy(); trial[axis] += direction * iteration['step']
            np.testing.assert_allclose(proposal['parameters'], wrap(trial), rtol=0, atol=1e-14)
        best = min(proposals, key=lambda call: call['objective_estimate'])
        margin = 2 * math.hypot(incumbent['estimated_standard_error'], best['estimated_standard_error'])
        improvement = incumbent['objective_estimate'] - best['objective_estimate']
        accepted = improvement > margin
        assert iteration['accepted'] == accepted
        assert iteration['best_proposal_evaluation'] == best['index']
        np.testing.assert_allclose([iteration['comparison_margin'], iteration['sampled_improvement']],
                                  [margin, improvement], rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-14)
        if accepted:
            accepted_indexes.add(best['index']); current = best; point = np.array(best['parameters'])
        else:
            current = incumbent
        np.testing.assert_allclose(iteration['parameters_after'], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-14)
        index += 9
    assert index == len(calls)
    assert {call['index'] for call in calls if call['accepted']} == accepted_indexes
    assert run['accepted_proposals'] == len(accepted_indexes)
    assert run['rejected_proposals'] == 96 - len(accepted_indexes)
    assert run['stop_reason'] == 'fixed_schedule_exhausted'
    np.testing.assert_allclose(run['parameters'], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-14)
    np.testing.assert_allclose([run['final_training_estimate'], run['final_training_standard_error']],
                              [current['objective_estimate'], current['estimated_standard_error']],
                              rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-14)
    return calls

The circuit audit separates initial reset, coherent work and terminal classical readout. Reset is a channel, not a unitary gate. The following NumPy interpreter uses explicit primitive matrices and bit permutations for the coherent suffix. It restores the separately recorded overall phase and uses the actual final qubit-to-classical map to compare classical distributions and unitary output rows. Checking only the cut mean would be insufficient: C4 symmetry can hide an incorrect wire permutation.

from functools import lru_cache

CLIFFORD_T = {'h', 'x', 'y', 'z', 's', 'sdg', 't', 'tdg', 'cx'}

@lru_cache(maxsize=128)
def primitive_matrix(name, angle=None):
    identity = np.eye(2, dtype=complex)
    x = np.array([[0, 1], [1, 0]], dtype=complex)
    y = np.array([[0, -1j], [1j, 0]], dtype=complex)
    z = np.diag([1., -1.]).astype(complex)
    fixed = {'h': np.array([[1, 1], [1, -1]], dtype=complex) / np.sqrt(2),
             'x': x, 'y': y, 'z': z,
             's': np.diag([1, 1j]), 'sdg': np.diag([1, -1j]),
             't': np.diag([1, np.exp(1j * np.pi / 4)]),
             'tdg': np.diag([1, np.exp(-1j * np.pi / 4)])}
    if name in fixed: return fixed[name]
    assert angle is not None and math.isfinite(angle)
    c, s = np.cos(angle / 2), np.sin(angle / 2)
    if name == 'rx': return c * identity - 1j * s * x
    if name == 'ry': return np.array([[c, -s], [s, c]], dtype=complex)
    if name == 'rz': return np.diag([np.exp(-1j * angle / 2), np.exp(1j * angle / 2)])
    raise ValueError(f'Unsupported primitive in independent interpreter: {name}')

def independent_qaoa_state(parameters):
    assert len(parameters) == 4
    state = np.ones(1 << WIDTH, dtype=complex) / np.sqrt(1 << WIDTH)
    for gamma, beta in zip(parameters[::2], parameters[1::2]):
        state *= np.exp(-1j * gamma * CUTS)
        for q in range(WIDTH):
            state = np.cos(beta) * state - 1j * np.sin(beta) * state[INDICES ^ (1 << q)]
    return state

def phase_aligned_error(actual, expected):
    overlap = np.vdot(expected, actual)
    phase = overlap / abs(overlap) if abs(overlap) else 1.
    return float(np.linalg.norm(actual - phase * expected)), phase




import ast
import re

def finite_angle_expression(text):
    tree = ast.parse(text, mode='eval')
    if sum(1 for _ in ast.walk(tree)) > 32:
        raise ValueError('Angle expression exceeds the restricted QASM audit domain')
    def scalar(node):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.value, (int, float)):
            return float(node.value)
        if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and node.id == 'pi': return math.pi
        if isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp) and isinstance(node.op, (ast.UAdd, ast.USub)):
            value = scalar(node.operand)
            return value if isinstance(node.op, ast.UAdd) else -value
        if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp) and isinstance(node.op, (ast.Add, ast.Sub, ast.Mult, ast.Div)):
            a, b = scalar(node.left), scalar(node.right)
            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Add): return a + b
            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Sub): return a - b
            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Mult): return a * b
            return a / b
        raise ValueError('Unsupported QASM angle expression')
    value = scalar(tree.body)
    if not math.isfinite(value): raise ValueError('QASM angle is not finite')
    return value

def primitive_qasm_operations(text):
    # This is a strict audit of our exported primitive subset, not a general
    # QASM compiler. Unknown declarations, gates or control flow are rejected.
    quantum, classical, operations, physical_wires = {}, {}, [], set()
    def operand(text, registers):
        physical = re.fullmatch(r'\$(\d+)', text.strip())
        if physical:
            number = int(physical.group(1))
            if registers is not quantum or not 0 <= number < WIDTH:
                raise ValueError('Invalid known routed physical-wire marker')
            physical_wires.add(number)
            return number
        match = re.fullmatch(r'([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*)\[(\d+)\]', text.strip())
        if not match: raise ValueError('Nonliteral QASM bit operand')
        name, number = match.group(1), int(match.group(2))
        if name not in registers or not 0 <= number < registers[name][1]:
            raise ValueError('QASM bit is outside its declared register')
        return registers[name][0] + number
    for original in text.splitlines():
        line = original.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith('//'): continue
        if line in {'OPENQASM 3.0;', 'include "stdgates.inc";'}: continue
        match = re.fullmatch(r'(qubit|bit)\[(\d+)\] ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*);', line)
        if match:
            registers = quantum if match.group(1) == 'qubit' else classical
            name, size = match.group(3), int(match.group(2))
            if name in registers: raise ValueError('Repeated QASM register')
            registers[name] = (sum(value[1] for value in registers.values()), size)
            continue
        match = re.fullmatch(r'(.+) = measure (.+);', line)
        if match:
            operations.append(['measure', [operand(match.group(2), quantum)],
                               [operand(match.group(1), classical)], []]); continue
        match = re.fullmatch(r'([a-z]+)(?:\(([^()]*)\))? (.+);', line)
        if not match: raise ValueError(f'Unsupported primitive QASM line: {line}')
        name, angle, wires_text = match.groups()
        if name not in CLIFFORD_T | {'rx', 'ry', 'rz', 'reset', 'barrier'}:
            raise ValueError(f'Unsupported primitive QASM operation: {name}')
        wires = [operand(token, quantum) for token in wires_text.split(',')]
        params = [finite_angle_expression(angle)] if name in {'rx', 'ry', 'rz'} else []
        if (angle is not None) != (name in {'rx', 'ry', 'rz'}):
            raise ValueError('Unexpected primitive QASM parameter')
        if name == 'cx' and len(wires) != 2: raise ValueError('Invalid QASM CX arity')
        if name not in {'cx', 'barrier'} and len(wires) != 1: raise ValueError('Invalid QASM primitive arity')
        operations.append([name, wires, [], params])
    if physical_wires:
        assert not quantum and physical_wires == set(range(WIDTH))
    else:
        assert sum(value[1] for value in quantum.values()) == WIDTH
    assert sum(value[1] for value in classical.values()) == WIDTH
    return operations

def coherent_operations_and_map(operations, saved_phase, *, require_resets=True):
    assert math.isfinite(saved_phase)
    operator = np.eye(1 << WIDTH, dtype=complex)
    initialized = set() if require_resets else set(range(WIDTH))
    measured, coherent_started, measure_started = [], False, False
    if not require_resets: assert not any(row[0] == 'reset' for row in operations)
    for name, wires, clbits, params in operations:
        if name == 'barrier': continue
        if name == 'reset':
            assert not coherent_started and not measure_started and len(wires) == 1
            assert wires[0] not in initialized and not clbits and not params
            initialized.add(wires[0]); continue
        if name == 'measure':
            assert coherent_started and initialized == set(range(WIDTH))
            assert len(wires) == len(clbits) == 1 and not params
            measure_started = True; measured.append((wires[0], clbits[0])); continue
        assert not measure_started and initialized == set(range(WIDTH)) and not clbits
        coherent_started = True
        if name == 'cx':
            assert len(wires) == 2 and wires[0] != wires[1] and not params
            control, target = wires
            permutation = INDICES.copy(); permutation[(INDICES & (1 << control)) != 0] ^= 1 << target
            operator = operator[permutation]
        else:
            assert len(wires) == 1
            assert len(params) == (1 if name in {'rx', 'ry', 'rz'} else 0)
            matrix = primitive_matrix(name, float(params[0]) if params else None)
            lo = INDICES[(INDICES & (1 << wires[0])) == 0]; hi = lo ^ (1 << wires[0])
            a, b = operator[lo].copy(), operator[hi].copy()
            operator[lo] = matrix[0, 0] * a + matrix[0, 1] * b
            operator[hi] = matrix[1, 0] * a + matrix[1, 1] * b
    assert initialized == set(range(WIDTH))
    assert len(measured) == WIDTH and {q for q, _ in measured} == {c for _, c in measured} == set(range(WIDTH))
    operator *= np.exp(1j * saved_phase)
    logical = np.empty_like(operator)
    for physical in INDICES:
        classical = sum(((physical >> q) & 1) << c for q, c in measured)
        logical[classical] = operator[physical]
    probabilities = np.abs(logical[:, 0]) ** 2
    np.testing.assert_allclose(probabilities.sum(), 1., rtol=0, atol=1e-10)
    return logical, probabilities, measured

import gzip
import io
import stat
import importlib.util

def canonical_digest(value):
    return digest_bytes(json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False).encode())

def artifact_path(name):
    if Path(name).is_absolute() or '..' in Path(name).parts:
        raise ValueError('Artifact references must be relative without parent traversal')
    lexical = artifact_folder / name
    if any(item.is_symlink() for item in [lexical, *lexical.parents] if item.is_relative_to(artifact_folder)):
        raise ValueError('Artifact references must not traverse symbolic links')
    target = lexical.resolve()
    if not target.is_relative_to(artifact_folder) or not target.is_file():
        raise ValueError('Artifact reference is not a regular saved file')
    return target

def saved_gzip_bytes(name, maximum=64 * 1024 * 1024):
    raw = artifact_path(name).read_bytes()
    with gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=io.BytesIO(raw)) as handle:
        expanded = handle.read(maximum + 1)
    if len(expanded) > maximum:
        raise ValueError('Expanded transport exceeds the bounded audit domain')
    return expanded, digest_bytes(raw)

def saved_gzip_json(name, maximum=64 * 1024 * 1024):
    expanded, sha = saved_gzip_bytes(name, maximum)
    return json.loads(expanded), sha

freeze, freeze_sha256 = read_json('freeze.json')

def import_pinned_snapshot(name, module_name):

import math
from fractions import Fraction


def reconcile_weighted_tv_transport(stored_tvs, replay_tvs, shots, saved_total, replay_total):
    """Audit a diagnostic sum; preserve every existing class/physical allowance.

    Products and ordered sums use IEEE binary64 round-to-nearest. Comparisons
    use exact binary rationals, with gamma_(2m) for m products plus m adds and
    an explicit absolute underflow term. These are arithmetic replay bounds,
    not new synthesis, transcript-distance or physical-failure budgets.
    """
    if not (1 <= len(shots) <= 64 and len(stored_tvs) == len(replay_tvs) == len(shots)):
        raise ValueError('Invalid bounded TV vectors')
    if (any(type(weight) is not int or not 1 <= weight <= 2**53 for weight in shots)
            or sum(shots) > 2**53):
        raise ValueError('Shots must be positive exactly representable binary64 integers')

    def finite_numbers(values, maximum):
        result = []
        for value in values:
            if (isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float))
                    or not math.isfinite(value) or not 0 <= value <= maximum):
                raise ValueError('Invalid finite nonnegative TV diagnostic')
            result.append(float(value))
        return result

    stored = finite_numbers(stored_tvs, 1)
    replay = finite_numbers(replay_tvs, 1)
    saved_value, replay_value = finite_numbers((saved_total, replay_total), sum(shots))
    for old, new in zip(stored, replay):
        # Same desired/reference orientation as the unchanged NumPy class check.
        if abs(old - new) > 2e-12 + 1e-7 * abs(new):
            raise AssertionError('Per-class TV replay left the existing tolerance')

    exact_stored = sum((weight * Fraction.from_float(value) for weight, value in zip(shots, stored)), Fraction())
    exact_replay = sum((weight * Fraction.from_float(value) for weight, value in zip(shots, replay)), Fraction())
    observed_transport = sum((weight * abs(Fraction.from_float(new) - Fraction.from_float(old))
                              for weight, old, new in zip(shots, stored, replay)), Fraction())
    operations = 2 * len(shots)
    unit_roundoff = Fraction(1, 2**53)
    denominator = 1 - operations * unit_roundoff
    gamma = operations * unit_roundoff / denominator
    underflow = Fraction(operations, 2**1075) / denominator
    stored_roundoff = gamma * exact_stored + underflow
    replay_roundoff = gamma * exact_replay + underflow
    stored_difference = abs(Fraction.from_float(saved_value) - exact_stored)
    replay_difference = abs(Fraction.from_float(replay_value) - exact_replay)
    if stored_difference > stored_roundoff:
        raise AssertionError('Stored aggregate differs from its exact weighted class inputs')
    if replay_difference > replay_roundoff:
        raise AssertionError('Replayed aggregate differs from its exact weighted class inputs')
    aggregate_difference = abs(Fraction.from_float(replay_value) - Fraction.from_float(saved_value))
    transport_bound = observed_transport + stored_roundoff + replay_roundoff
    if aggregate_difference > transport_bound:
        raise AssertionError('Aggregate drift exceeds observed weighted TV transport and roundoff')
    return {'observed_shot_weighted_tv_transport': float(observed_transport),
            'stored_aggregate_roundoff_bound': float(stored_roundoff),
            'replayed_aggregate_roundoff_bound': float(replay_roundoff),
            'aggregate_difference': float(aggregate_difference),
            'transport_bound': float(transport_bound),
            'exact_binary_rational_comparisons': True,
            'scope': 'diagnostic host transport; all class, realization and physical budgets unchanged'}


def expected_recorded_source_operations(parameters):
    values = [['h', [q], [], []] for q in range(WIDTH)]
    for gamma, beta in zip(parameters[::2], parameters[1::2]):

            values += [['cx', [u, v], [], []], ['rz', [v], [], [-gamma]], ['cx', [u, v], [], []]]
        values += [['rx', [q], [], [2 * beta]] for q in range(WIDTH)]
    values += [['barrier', list(range(WIDTH)), [], []]]
    values += [['measure', [q], [q], []] for q in range(WIDTH)]
    return values

    matrices, probabilities, per_stage = {}, {}, {}
    for prefix, role in (('source', 'augmented_source'), ('routed', 'routed'), ('clifford_t', 'clifford_t')):
        reference = meta['circuits'][role]

This notebook is designed to audit the saved sixth optimization study without repeating its training. The frozen plan contains 36 ideal sampled runs and 24 deterministic CPU controls. Every start, seed, rejection, missed target, and inconclusive final interval is retained. Until matching completed artifacts are present, notebook execution stops instead of generating study data.

The cases are C4/C6 QAOA at depths one and two, and four-/six-spin open-chain VQE. Two prescribed starts per case distinguish initialization behavior, while exact-objective and expected-margin controls help inspect sampling and acceptance effects. These bounded controls do not certify the best achievable ansatz energy or general optimizer convergence. Equal preparation counts still permit different gate workloads and hardware costs.

records.content:
The bounded checks below enumerate cycle cuts independently, build each spin-chain Hamiltonian as a dense matrix, and apply rotations and entangling permutations directly to amplitude vectors. They use Qiskit’s little-endian wire convention. Group population variances include covariance among every term scored from the same bitstring. These classical calculations are numerical checks, not formal proofs.

cut_cache={}
hamiltonian_cache={}


def independent_cuts(n_qubits,edges):
    if not 2<=n_qubits<=6:
        raise ValueError("independent classical checks are capped at 6 qubits")
    key=(n_qubits,tuple(sorted(tuple(sorted(edge)) for edge in edges)))
    if key not in cut_cache:
        cut_cache[key]=np.array([sum(((z>>u)&1)!=((z>>v)&1) for u,v in edges)
                                 for z in range(1<<n_qubits)],dtype=float)
    return cut_cache[key]


def independent_qaoa_state(n_qubits,edges,parameters):
    values=independent_cuts(n_qubits,edges)
    if len(parameters)%2 or not parameters:
        raise ValueError("QAOA uses interleaved gamma,beta pairs")
    state=np.ones(1<<n_qubits,dtype=complex)/np.sqrt(1<<n_qubits)
    indices=np.arange(1<<n_qubits)
    for gamma,beta in zip(parameters[::2],parameters[1::2]):
        state*=np.exp(-1j*gamma*values)
        for wire in range(n_qubits):
            # Simultaneous amplitudes implement exp(-i beta X) independently.
            state=np.cos(beta)*state-1j*np.sin(beta)*state[indices^(1<<wire)]
    np.testing.assert_allclose(np.vdot(state,state).real,1.,rtol=0,atol=1e-12)
    return state


def independent_chain_hamiltonian(n_qubits):
    if not 2<=n_qubits<=6:
        raise ValueError("these dense VQE checks are limited to declared n<=6 cases")
    if n_qubits not in hamiltonian_cache:
        indices=np.arange(1<<n_qubits)
        z_values=np.array([-sum(1-2*((z>>q)&1) for q in range(n_qubits))
                           for z in indices],dtype=float)
        matrix=np.diag(z_values)
        for q in range(n_qubits-1):
            matrix+=.5*np.eye(1<<n_qubits)[:,indices^((1<<q)|(1<<(q+1)))]
        np.testing.assert_allclose(matrix,matrix.T,rtol=0,atol=1e-14)
        hamiltonian_cache[n_qubits]=(matrix,float(np.linalg.eigvalsh(matrix)[0]))
    return hamiltonian_cache[n_qubits]


def independent_chain_state(n_qubits,parameters):
    if len(parameters)!=n_qubits or not 2<=n_qubits<=6:
        raise ValueError("one RY angle per qubit is required for these declared cases")
    indices=np.arange(1<<n_qubits)
    state=np.zeros(1<<n_qubits,dtype=complex)
    state[0]=1
    for q,theta in enumerate(parameters):
        zeros=indices[(indices&(1<<q))==0]
        ones=zeros^(1<<q)
        before=state.copy()
        state[zeros]=np.cos(theta/2)*before[zeros]-np.sin(theta/2)*before[ones]
        state[ones]=np.sin(theta/2)*before[zeros]+np.cos(theta/2)*before[ones]
    for q in range(n_qubits-1):
        permutation=indices.copy()
        permutation[(indices&(1<<q))!=0]^=1<<(q+1)
        state=state[permutation]
    np.testing.assert_allclose(np.vdot(state,state).real,1.,rtol=0,atol=1e-12)
    return state


def independent_group_scores(algorithm,n_qubits,edges,group_name):
    if algorithm=="qaoa":
        return independent_cuts(n_qubits,edges)
    if group_name=="all_z":
        return np.array([-sum(1-2*((z>>q)&1) for q in range(n_qubits))
                         for z in range(1<<n_qubits)],dtype=float)
    if group_name=="all_x":
        return np.array([.5*sum((1-2*((z>>q)&1))*(1-2*((z>>(q+1))&1)) for q in range(n_qubits-1))
                         for z in range(1<<n_qubits)],dtype=float)
    raise ValueError("unexpected measurement group")


def independent_group_state(algorithm, n_qubits, edges, parameters, group_name):
    state = (independent_qaoa_state(n_qubits, edges, parameters) if algorithm == "qaoa"
             else independent_chain_state(n_qubits, parameters))
    if group_name == "all_x":
        indices = np.arange(1 << n_qubits)
        for wire in range(n_qubits):
            zeros = indices[(indices & (1 << wire)) == 0]
            ones = zeros ^ (1 << wire)
            before = state.copy()
            state[zeros] = (before[zeros] + before[ones]) / np.sqrt(2)
            state[ones] = (before[zeros] - before[ones]) / np.sqrt(2)
    elif group_name != "all_z":
        raise ValueError("unexpected measurement group")
    return state


def independent_group_moments(algorithm, n_qubits, edges, parameters, group_name):
    state = independent_group_state(algorithm, n_qubits, edges, parameters, group_name)
    scores = independent_group_scores(algorithm, n_qubits, edges, group_name)
    probabilities = np.abs(state) ** 2
    mean = float(probabilities @ scores)
    variance = float(probabilities @ (scores - mean) ** 2)
    return mean, variance


def interval_status(algorithm, value, radius):
    if algorithm == "qaoa":
        return "supported" if value - radius >= .80 else "missed" if value + radius < .80 else "inconclusive"
    return "supported" if value + radius <= .05 else "missed" if value - radius > .05 else "inconclusive"



def replay_search(run, initial, *, control=False):
    """Reconstruct the fixed polling order, decisions and final annotations."""
    calls = run["evaluations"]
    dimension = len(initial)
    assert len(calls) == 1 + 12 * (1 + 2 * dimension)
    assert [call["index"] for call in calls] == list(range(len(calls)))
    assert calls[0]["role"] == "initial" and not calls[0]["accepted"]
    point = (np.asarray(initial, dtype=float) + np.pi) % (2 * np.pi) - np.pi
    np.testing.assert_allclose(calls[0]["parameters"], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
    mean_key = "objective_mean" if control else "objective_estimate"
    se_key = "effective_standard_error" if control else "estimated_standard_error"
    expected_index, current = 1, calls[0]
    accepted_indexes = set()
    for index, iteration in enumerate(run["iterations"]):
        assert iteration["index"] == index and iteration["step"] == (.4, .2, .1)[index // 4]
        assert iteration["incumbent_evaluation"] == expected_index
        expected_proposals = list(range(expected_index + 1, expected_index + 1 + 2 * dimension))
        assert iteration["proposal_evaluations"] == expected_proposals
        incumbent = calls[expected_index]
        proposals = [calls[item] for item in expected_proposals]
        assert incumbent["role"] == "incumbent" and not incumbent["accepted"]
        assert [(proposal["axis"], proposal["direction"]) for proposal in proposals] == [
            (axis, direction) for axis in range(dimension) for direction in (-1, 1)]
        np.testing.assert_allclose(iteration["parameters_before"], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(incumbent["parameters"], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
        for proposal in proposals:
            assert proposal["role"] == "proposal"
            if control:
                assert proposal["iteration_index"] == incumbent["iteration_index"] == index
            expected = point.copy()
            expected[proposal["axis"]] += proposal["direction"] * iteration["step"]
            expected = (expected + np.pi) % (2 * np.pi) - np.pi
            np.testing.assert_allclose(proposal["parameters"], expected, rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
        # Python min keeps the first minimum in the frozen polling order.
        best = min(proposals, key=lambda call: call[mean_key])
        margin = 2 * math.hypot(incumbent[se_key], best[se_key])
        improvement = incumbent[mean_key] - best[mean_key]
        accepted = improvement > margin
        assert accepted == iteration["accepted"]
        assert best["index"] == iteration["best_proposal_evaluation"]
        np.testing.assert_allclose(iteration["comparison_margin"], margin, rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-14)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(iteration["exact_improvement" if control else "sampled_improvement"],
                                  improvement, rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-14)
        for proposal in proposals:
            assert proposal["accepted"] == (accepted and proposal["index"] == best["index"])
        if accepted: accepted_indexes.add(best["index"])
        current = best if accepted else incumbent
        point = np.asarray(current["parameters"])
        np.testing.assert_allclose(iteration["parameters_after"], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
        expected_index += 1 + 2 * dimension
    assert len(run["iterations"]) == 12 and expected_index == len(calls)
    assert run["accepted_proposals"] == len(accepted_indexes)
    assert run["rejected_proposals"] == 24 * dimension - len(accepted_indexes)
    assert {call["index"] for call in calls if call["accepted"]} == accepted_indexes
    assert run["convergence_certified"] is False
    np.testing.assert_allclose(run["parameters"], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
    if control:
        assert run["final_evaluation"] == current["index"]
        np.testing.assert_allclose(run["final_parameters"], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
        np.testing.assert_allclose([run["final_exact_objective"], run["final_effective_standard_error"],
                                   run["final_expected_standard_error"]],
                                  [current["objective_mean"], current["effective_standard_error"],
                                   current["expected_standard_error"]], rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-14)
    else:
        np.testing.assert_allclose([run["final_training_estimate"], run["final_training_standard_error"]],
                                  [current["objective_estimate"], current["estimated_standard_error"]],
                                  rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-14)


def independent_quality(case, parameters, diagnostic):
    algorithm, width = case["algorithm"], case["n_qubits"]
    edges = tuple(tuple(edge) for edge in case.get("edges", ()))
    if algorithm == "qaoa":
        values = independent_cuts(width, edges)
        optimum = float(values.max())
        state = independent_qaoa_state(width, edges, parameters)
        raw_quality = float(np.abs(state) ** 2 @ values)
        quality = raw_quality / optimum
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(diagnostic["cut_values"], values)
        np.testing.assert_allclose([diagnostic["classical_optimum"], diagnostic["exact_expected_cut"],
                                   diagnostic["exact_approximation_ratio"]],
                                  [optimum, raw_quality, quality], rtol=0, atol=1e-10)
        return quality, optimum, None, quality >= .80
    matrix, ground = independent_chain_hamiltonian(width)
    state = independent_chain_state(width, parameters)
    raw_quality = float(np.vdot(state, matrix @ state).real)
    quality = (raw_quality - ground) / width
    np.testing.assert_allclose([diagnostic["ground_energy"], diagnostic["exact_energy"], diagnostic["energy_density_gap"]],
                              [ground, raw_quality, quality], rtol=0, atol=1e-10)
    return quality, width, ground, quality <= .05

for case in study["cases"]:
    algorithm, width = case["algorithm"], case["n_qubits"]

        assert run["objective_evaluations"] == 1 + 12 * (1 + 2 * len(expected_initial))
        assert run["total_shots"] == 65_648
        assert run["exact_diagnostics_used_for_optimization"] is False
        expected_shots = {0: initial_shots}
        for iteration_index, iteration in enumerate(run["iterations"]):
            shots = base * (2 ** (iteration_index // 4))
            for index in [iteration["incumbent_evaluation"], *iteration["proposal_evaluations"]]:
