        assert set(expected_shots) == set(range(len(run["evaluations"])))
        weighted = Counter()
        for phase_index, phase, calls in ((0, "training", run["evaluations"]), (1, "validation", [run["validation"]])):
            for evaluation_index, call in enumerate(calls):
                total_calls += 1
                assert call["total_shots"] == sum(group["shots"] for group in call["groups"])
                assert [group["group"] for group in call["groups"]] == case["groups"]
                means, mean_variances = [], []
                for group_index, group in enumerate(call["groups"]):
                    assert group["shots"] == (expected_shots[evaluation_index] if phase == "training" else 16_384)
                    scores = independent_group_scores(algorithm, width, edges, group["group"])
                    counts = np.zeros(1 << width, dtype=np.int64)
                    for bits, number in group["counts"].items():
                        assert len(bits) == width and set(bits) <= {"0", "1"}
                        assert isinstance(number, int) and not isinstance(number, bool) and number > 0
                        counts[int(bits, 2)] = number
                    assert counts.sum() == group["shots"]
                    mean = float(counts @ scores / group["shots"])
                    variance = float(counts @ (scores - mean) ** 2 / (group["shots"] - 1))
                    se = math.sqrt(variance / group["shots"])
                    np.testing.assert_allclose([group["estimate"], group["sample_variance"], group["estimated_standard_error"]],
                                              [mean, variance, se], rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12)
                    expected_range = (0., float(len(edges))) if algorithm == "qaoa" else ((-width, width) if group["group"] == "all_z" else (-(width - 1) / 2, (width - 1) / 2))
                    np.testing.assert_allclose([group["outcome_min"], group["outcome_max"]], expected_range, rtol=0, atol=1e-14)
                    means.append(mean); mean_variances.append(variance / group["shots"])
                    stream = (run["seed"], start["stream_id"], phase_index, evaluation_index, group_index)
                    assert tuple(group["rng"]["stream_key"]) == stream and stream not in seen_streams
                    assert group["rng"]["entropy"] == [run["seed"], start["stream_id"]]
                    assert group["rng"]["spawn_key"] == [phase_index, evaluation_index, group_index]
                    seen_streams.add(stream)
                    counts_ops = {name: number for name, number in group["circuit_gate_counts"].items() if name != "barrier"}
                    if algorithm == "qaoa":
                        expected_ops = {"h": width, "rz": len(edges) * case["p"], "rx": width * case["p"],
                                        "cx": 2 * len(edges) * case["p"], "measure": width}
                    else:
                        expected_ops = {"ry": width, "cx": width - 1, "measure": width}
                        if group["group"] == "all_x": expected_ops["h"] = width
                    assert counts_ops == expected_ops
                    weighted.update({gate: number * group["shots"] for gate, number in counts_ops.items()})
                    measured_trace.append({"case": case, "run": run, "phase": phase,
                                           "evaluation_index": evaluation_index, "group_index": group_index,
                                           "call": call, "group": group})
                    total_groups += 1; total_shots += group["shots"]
                expected_mean = -sum(means) if algorithm == "qaoa" else sum(means)
                np.testing.assert_allclose(call["objective_estimate"], expected_mean, rtol=0, atol=1e-11)
                np.testing.assert_allclose(call["estimated_standard_error"], math.sqrt(sum(mean_variances)), rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12)
        replay_search(run, expected_initial)
        quality, denominator, ground, exact_met = independent_quality(case, run["parameters"], run["diagnostic"])
        assert run["target_met_audit"] == exact_met
        validation = run["validation"]
        np.testing.assert_allclose(validation["parameters"], run["parameters"], rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
        assert validation["total_shots"] == group_count * 16_384
        radius = sum((group["outcome_max"] - group["outcome_min"]) * math.sqrt(math.log(2 / (.05 / 48)) / (2 * group["shots"]))

        bound = validation["quality_bound"]
        np.testing.assert_allclose([bound["normalized_estimate"], bound["simultaneous_radius"]], [estimate, radius], rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
        assert bound["target_status"] == interval_status(algorithm, estimate, radius)
        assert bound["precision_supported"] == (radius <= .05)
        all_gate_counts.update(weighted)
        run_rows.append({"case": case, "run": run, "quality": quality, "exact_met": exact_met,
                         "estimate": estimate, "radius": radius, "status": bound["target_status"],
                         "weighted_counts": dict(weighted), "total_shots": run["total_shots"] + validation["total_shots"]})
assert namespaces == set(range(30, 42))
assert len(run_rows) == 36
assert (total_calls, total_groups, total_shots) == (3_672, 5_280, 3_149_760)
print({"retained_sampled_runs": len(run_rows), "replayed_sampled_sweeps": 432,
       "reconstructed_calls": total_calls, "measured_groups": total_groups,

control_rows = []

        for index in [iteration["incumbent_evaluation"], *iteration["proposal_evaluations"]]:

        assert call["quantum_preparations"] == 0 and call["count_samples"] is None
        assert call["seed"] is None

        assert [group["group"] for group in call["groups"]] == case["groups"]

Fresh final groups receive Hoeffding intervals using the frozen family allocation \delta_{\rm group}=0.05/48. Their target statuses distinguish support, misses and inconclusive intervals. They cover selected-state expectations conditional on training under ideal independent sampling; they do not certify training decisions or convergence.

The complete logical workload includes input preparation gates, objective interactions, measurement basis changes, rejected proposals and readout. Exact QASM deduplication is an export convenience and does not remove repeated preparations. Rotation synthesis, physical initialization/reset, routing and hardware feedback remain unmodeled. No physical projections are requested in this increment.

Classical C4 reference coverage only. The existing Lean result does not prove these QAOA/VQE circuits, stochastic decisions, control comparisons, or resource ledgers.

    assert saved_ledger[key] == ledger[key], key

The plots retain every prescribed sampled seed and both CPU control modes. Their exact values are independent post-training diagnostics; the final confidence flags remain separate. The decision-count plot records twelve fixed sweeps, not a convergence test. Exact-objective and expected-margin controls are different deterministic search paths, and the expected-margin path is not the expectation of a stochastic optimizer.

Preparation bars show actual sampled training and holdout counts. CPU control virtual allocations do not add quantum preparations. Source CX counts include every actual group’s repetitions and therefore remain different even at equal training preparation counts.

The triangle has edges (0,1),(1,2),(0,2). The task maximizes C(z)=\sum_{(u,v)}[z_u\ne z_v], and training minimizes the negative sampled cut mean. Enumerating all eight assignments gives maximum cut two. Bitstrings read q_2q_1q_0.

QAOA prepares |+\rangle^{\otimes3} with H on all three qubits. It uses CX–RZ(−\gamma)–CX on each edge and RX(2\beta) on every qubit. Angles are radians with R_P(\alpha)=e^{-i\alpha P/2}. A single all-Z group scores all three edges jointly. The cycle’s earlier scalar energy formula does not apply to this graph; below we independently apply the diagonal cost phase and an explicit NumPy tensor-product mixer.

For VQE, the new dimensionless Hamiltonian isH=-0.8Z_0-0.6Z_1+0.4X_0X_1.

The ansatz still prepares |00\rangle, applies RY(\theta) on qubit zero, then CX(0,1). One joint all-Z group scores -0.8Z_0-0.6Z_1, retaining covariance; the all-X group scores 0.4X_0X_1 after H basis changes on both qubits. Every shot needs a fresh preparation.

The post-run reference ground energy is -\sqrt{2.12}. The ansatz expectation is E(\theta)=-1.4\cos\theta+0.4\sin\theta. Full matrix diagonalization below checks the reference rather than assuming that the ansatz subspace contains the global minimum.

The rule is a fixed-budget heuristic, not a calibrated significance test or a convergence certificate. After the schedule ends, each final state receives fresh validation with 4,096 shots per group. Validation and exact audits do not choose training moves.

The predeclared post-run targets are expected triangle cut at least 1.90 and exact VQE energy gap at most 0.03 above -\sqrt{2.12}. These refer to exact post-run quality, not uncertainty on the sampled estimate. All seeds retain the same initial point per task. Algorithm IDs 2 and 3 distinguish the new tasks from earlier random streams; PCG64 uses SeedSequence([seed, algorithm_id], spawn_key=(family, call_index, group_index)), with family zero for training and one for validation. edges = ((0, 1), (1, 2), (0, 2))
n_qubits = 3
cut_values = np.array([sum(((z >> u) & 1) != ((z >> v) & 1) for u, v in edges)
                       for z in range(1 << n_qubits)], dtype=float)
np.testing.assert_array_equal(cut_values, opt.maxcut_values(n_qubits, edges))
assert cut_values.max() == 2
I = np.eye(2)
X = np.array([[0., 1.], [1., 0.]])
Z = np.diag([1., -1.])
reference_hamiltonian = -.8*np.kron(I, Z) - .6*np.kron(Z, I) + .4*np.kron(X, X)
np.testing.assert_allclose(portable["vqe"]["reference"]["matrix"], reference_hamiltonian, rtol=0, atol=1e-14)
assert {tuple(edge) for edge in portable["qaoa"]["edges"]} == set(edges)

reference_energy = float(reference_spectrum[0])
np.testing.assert_allclose(reference_energy, -np.sqrt(2.12), rtol=0, atol=1e-14)


def triangle_reference(parameters):
    gamma, beta = parameters
    # An independent 8-dimensional application of exp(-i gamma C).
    state = np.ones(8, dtype=complex)/np.sqrt(8)
    state *= np.exp(-1j*gamma*cut_values)
    rx = np.cos(beta)*I - 1j*np.sin(beta)*X
    mixer = np.kron(rx, np.kron(rx, rx))
    state = mixer @ state
    return float((np.abs(state)**2) @ cut_values)


# These fixed reference checks are separate from optimizer decisions.
for angles in ((.2, .1), (-.6, .3), (.8, -.2)):
    circuit_state = Statevector.from_instruction(opt.build_qaoa_circuit(n_qubits, edges, [angles[0]], [angles[1]]))
    np.testing.assert_allclose(circuit_state.probabilities() @ cut_values, triangle_reference(angles), rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
print({"triangle_maximum_cut": float(cut_values.max()),
       "maximum_cut_bitstrings": [f"{z:03b}" for z in np.flatnonzero(cut_values == 2)],
       "new_Hamiltonian_spectrum": reference_spectrum.tolist(), "ground_energy": reference_energy})

The following check reconstructs every observed mean and sample variance from its measured counts. It then replays the parameter decisions using only measured estimates, standard errors and the prescribed margin. Exact audit fields are excluded from this replay.

All rejected proposals remain in the record and count toward the workload. Re-estimating the incumbent means the displayed sampled trajectory need not be monotone, even when accepted parameter updates appear favorable. The main chapter’s native MyST table is generated independently by the sampled artifact script; this notebook reports its own fresh execution.

def outcome_score(algorithm, group, bits):
    z = int(bits, 2)
    if algorithm == "qaoa":
        return float(sum(((z >> u) & 1) != ((z >> v) & 1) for u, v in edges))
    if group["group"] == "all_z":
        return -.8*(1 - 2*((z >> 0) & 1)) - .6*(1 - 2*((z >> 1) & 1))
    return .4*(1 - 2*((z >> 0) & 1))*(1 - 2*((z >> 1) & 1))


seen_stream_keys = set()
for algorithm in ("qaoa", "vqe"):
    dimension = 2 if algorithm == "qaoa" else 1
    expected_training_calls = 1 + 32*(1 + 2*dimension)
    expected_training_shots = (1 if algorithm == "qaoa" else 2)*(256 + (1 + 2*dimension)*8*(256 + 512 + 1024 + 2048))
    for run in portable[algorithm]["runs"]:
        assert run["objective_evaluations"] == expected_training_calls
        assert run["iteration_count"] == 32
        assert run["stop_reason"] == "fixed_schedule_exhausted"
        assert run["total_shots"] == expected_training_shots
        calls = run["evaluations"]
        for call in calls + [run["validation"]]:
            means, mean_variances = [], []
            for group in call["groups"]:
                assert sum(group["counts"].values()) == group["shots"]
                assert group["rng"]["entropy"] == [run["seed"], 2 if algorithm == "qaoa" else 3]
                stream_key = tuple(group["rng"]["stream_key"])
                assert stream_key not in seen_stream_keys
                seen_stream_keys.add(stream_key)
                mean = sum(count*outcome_score(algorithm, group, bits)
                           for bits, count in group["counts"].items()) / group["shots"]
                variance = sum(count*(outcome_score(algorithm, group, bits) - mean)**2
                               for bits, count in group["counts"].items()) / (group["shots"] - 1)
                np.testing.assert_allclose(mean, group["estimate"], rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
                np.testing.assert_allclose(variance, group["sample_variance"], rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12)
                means.append(mean)
                mean_variances.append(variance/group["shots"])
            signed_mean = -sum(means) if algorithm == "qaoa" else sum(means)
            np.testing.assert_allclose(signed_mean, call["objective_estimate"], rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
            np.testing.assert_allclose(np.sqrt(sum(mean_variances)), call["estimated_standard_error"], rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12)
        point = (np.array(run["initial"]) + np.pi) % (2*np.pi) - np.pi
        for iteration in run["iterations"]:
            incumbent = calls[iteration["incumbent_evaluation"]]
            proposals = [calls[index] for index in iteration["proposal_evaluations"]]
            np.testing.assert_allclose(incumbent["parameters"], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
            best = min(proposals, key=lambda item: item["objective_estimate"])
            margin = 2*np.hypot(incumbent["estimated_standard_error"], best["estimated_standard_error"])
            accepted = incumbent["objective_estimate"] - best["objective_estimate"] > margin
            assert accepted == iteration["accepted"]
            assert best["index"] == iteration["best_proposal_evaluation"]
            if accepted:
                point = np.array(best["parameters"])
            np.testing.assert_allclose(iteration["parameters_after"], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(run["parameters"], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
        assert all(group["rng"]["spawn_key"][0] == 0 for call in calls for group in call["groups"])
        assert all(group["rng"]["spawn_key"][0] == 1 for group in run["validation"]["groups"])
print("Reconstructed all 780 training/validation objective calls from counts and replayed all 192 sampled sweeps.")

For QAOA, the graphs are paths and cycles with n=3,4,5,6,8 vertices, at p=1,2 layers. Each instance uses seeds 7, 19, and 41, giving 60 runs. Every layer starts at (\gamma_j,\beta_j)=(0.2,0.1); parameters are recorded in interleaved layer order. The circuit starts with H on every qubit, uses CX–RZ(−\gamma_j)–CX for each edge, and RX(2\beta_j) for mixing. The optimizer minimizes the negative joint cut mean. Its post-run target is exact expected cut divided by the classical maximum, at least 0.80.

For VQE, n=2,3,4,6 and the open-chain Hamiltonian isH=-\sum_{q=0}^{n-1}Z_q+\frac12\sum_{q=0}^{n-2}X_qX_{q+1}.

The single ansatz layer applies RY(\theta_q) on every zero-initialized qubit, followed by the chain CX(0,1), CX(1,2), …, CX(n-2,n-1). Every angle starts at 0.6 radians for each of the same three seeds, giving 12 runs. A joint all-Z group scores -\sum Z_q; an independent all-X group scores \tfrac12\sum X_qX_{q+1}. Group score variances retain covariance of all terms sharing a basis. The post-run target is exact energy-density gap (E-E_0)/n at most 0.05.

The normalized outputs are different computational tasks, not interchangeable scores. A larger ansatz adds gates and parameters and therefore changes workload; observed quality improvement is not a matched physical resource improvement.

records.content:
The checks below enumerate each graph’s cut values independently, construct each chain Hamiltonian as a full small matrix, and reconstruct every measured group mean and variance from counts. They replay all decisions using only sampled estimates and estimated standard errors. Exact state expectations and ground energies are inspected after training, with no influence on accepted moves.

All states use Qiskit’s little-endian wire convention. The largest classical reference is bounded by the declared small instances. Numerical references are independent checks of these runs, not formal correctness or general convergence proofs.

cut_cache={}
hamiltonian_cache={}


def independent_cuts(n_qubits,edges):
    if not 2<=n_qubits<=8:
        raise ValueError("independent classical checks are capped at 8 qubits")
    key=(n_qubits,tuple(sorted(tuple(sorted(edge)) for edge in edges)))
    if key not in cut_cache:
        cut_cache[key]=np.array([sum(((z>>u)&1)!=((z>>v)&1) for u,v in edges)
                                 for z in range(1<<n_qubits)],dtype=float)
    return cut_cache[key]


def independent_qaoa_state(n_qubits,edges,parameters):
    values=independent_cuts(n_qubits,edges)
    if len(parameters)%2 or not parameters:
        raise ValueError("QAOA uses interleaved gamma,beta pairs")
    state=np.ones(1<<n_qubits,dtype=complex)/np.sqrt(1<<n_qubits)
    indices=np.arange(1<<n_qubits)
    for gamma,beta in zip(parameters[::2],parameters[1::2]):
        state*=np.exp(-1j*gamma*values)
        for wire in range(n_qubits):
            # Simultaneous amplitudes implement exp(-i beta X) independently.
            state=np.cos(beta)*state-1j*np.sin(beta)*state[indices^(1<<wire)]
    np.testing.assert_allclose(np.vdot(state,state).real,1.,rtol=0,atol=1e-12)
    return state


def independent_chain_hamiltonian(n_qubits):
    if not 2<=n_qubits<=6:
        raise ValueError("these dense VQE checks are limited to declared n<=6 cases")
    if n_qubits not in hamiltonian_cache:
        indices=np.arange(1<<n_qubits)
        z_values=np.array([-sum(1-2*((z>>q)&1) for q in range(n_qubits))
                           for z in indices],dtype=float)
        matrix=np.diag(z_values)
        for q in range(n_qubits-1):
            matrix+=.5*np.eye(1<<n_qubits)[:,indices^((1<<q)|(1<<(q+1)))]
        np.testing.assert_allclose(matrix,matrix.T,rtol=0,atol=1e-14)
        hamiltonian_cache[n_qubits]=(matrix,float(np.linalg.eigvalsh(matrix)[0]))
    return hamiltonian_cache[n_qubits]


def independent_chain_state(n_qubits,parameters):
    if len(parameters)!=n_qubits or not 2<=n_qubits<=6:
        raise ValueError("one RY angle per qubit is required for these declared cases")
    indices=np.arange(1<<n_qubits)
    state=np.zeros(1<<n_qubits,dtype=complex)
    state[0]=1
    for q,theta in enumerate(parameters):
        zeros=indices[(indices&(1<<q))==0]
        ones=zeros^(1<<q)
        before=state.copy()
        state[zeros]=np.cos(theta/2)*before[zeros]-np.sin(theta/2)*before[ones]
        state[ones]=np.sin(theta/2)*before[zeros]+np.cos(theta/2)*before[ones]
    for q in range(n_qubits-1):
        permutation=indices.copy()
        permutation[(indices&(1<<q))!=0]^=1<<(q+1)
        state=state[permutation]
    np.testing.assert_allclose(np.vdot(state,state).real,1.,rtol=0,atol=1e-12)
    return state


def independent_group_scores(algorithm,n_qubits,edges,group_name):
    if algorithm=="qaoa":
        return independent_cuts(n_qubits,edges)
    if group_name=="all_z":
        return np.array([-sum(1-2*((z>>q)&1) for q in range(n_qubits))
                         for z in range(1<<n_qubits)],dtype=float)
    if group_name=="all_x":
        return np.array([.5*sum((1-2*((z>>q)&1))*(1-2*((z>>(q+1))&1)) for q in range(n_qubits-1))
                         for z in range(1<<n_qubits)],dtype=float)
    raise ValueError("unexpected measurement group")




from collections import Counter
run_rows=[]
seen_stream_keys=set()
total_calls=total_groups=total_shots=0
all_gate_counts=Counter()
score_cache={}


def interval_status(algorithm,value,radius):
    if algorithm=="qaoa":
        return "supported" if value-radius>=.80 else "missed" if value+radius<.80 else "inconclusive"
    return "supported" if value+radius<=.05 else "missed" if value-radius>.05 else "inconclusive"


assert len(study["cases"])==24
for case in study["cases"]:
    algorithm=case["algorithm"]
    width=case["n_qubits"]
    edges=tuple(tuple(edge) for edge in case.get("edges",()))
    expected_initial=[x for _ in range(case["p"]) for x in (.2,.1)] if algorithm=="qaoa" else [.6]*width
    np.testing.assert_allclose(case["initial"],expected_initial,rtol=0,atol=1e-14)
    assert [run["seed"] for run in case["runs"]]==[7,19,41]
    groups_per_call=1 if algorithm=="qaoa" else 2
    dimension=len(expected_initial)
    expected_training_calls=1+(1+2*dimension)*12
    expected_training_shots=groups_per_call*(128+(1+2*dimension)*4*(256+512+1024))
    for run in case["runs"]:
        assert run["objective_evaluations"]==expected_training_calls
        assert run["iteration_count"]==12
        assert run["stop_reason"]=="fixed_schedule_exhausted"
        assert run["total_shots"]==expected_training_shots
        assert run["validation"]["total_shots"]==groups_per_call*16384
        assert run["exact_diagnostics_used_for_optimization"] is False
        np.testing.assert_allclose(run["initial"],expected_initial,rtol=0,atol=1e-14)
        weighted=Counter()
        for phase,calls in ((0,run["evaluations"]),(1,[run["validation"]])):
            for call in calls:
                total_calls+=1
                assert call["total_shots"]==sum(g["shots"] for g in call["groups"])
                assert [g["group"] for g in call["groups"]]==case["groups"]
                means,mean_variances=[],[]
                for group in call["groups"]:
                    key=(case["case_id"],group["group"])
                    if key not in score_cache:
                        score_cache[key]=independent_group_scores(algorithm,width,edges,group["group"])
                    scores=score_cache[key]
                    counts=np.zeros(1<<width,dtype=int)
                    for bits,count in group["counts"].items(): counts[int(bits,2)]=count
                    assert counts.sum()==group["shots"]
                    mean=float(counts@scores/group["shots"])
                    variance=float(counts@((scores-mean)**2)/(group["shots"]-1))
                    np.testing.assert_allclose([group["estimate"],group["sample_variance"]],
                                               [mean,variance],rtol=1e-12,atol=1e-12)
                    assert group["outcome_min"]<=scores.min() and group["outcome_max"]>=scores.max()
                    means.append(mean);mean_variances.append(variance/group["shots"])
                    assert group["rng"]["entropy"]==[run["seed"],case["stream_id"]]
                    assert group["rng"]["spawn_key"][0]==phase
                    stream=tuple(group["rng"]["stream_key"])
                    assert stream not in seen_stream_keys
                    seen_stream_keys.add(stream)
                    count_ops={k:v for k,v in group["circuit_gate_counts"].items() if k!="barrier"}
                    if algorithm=="qaoa":
                        expected_ops={"h":width,"rz":len(edges)*case["p"],"rx":width*case["p"],
                                      "cx":2*len(edges)*case["p"],"measure":width}
                    else:
                        expected_ops={"ry":width,"cx":width-1,"measure":width}
                        if group["group"]=="all_x": expected_ops["h"]=width
                    assert count_ops==expected_ops
                    weighted.update({gate:number*group["shots"] for gate,number in count_ops.items()})
                    total_groups+=1;total_shots+=group["shots"]
                signed_mean=-sum(means) if algorithm=="qaoa" else sum(means)
                np.testing.assert_allclose(call["objective_estimate"],signed_mean,rtol=0,atol=1e-11)
                np.testing.assert_allclose(call["estimated_standard_error"],np.sqrt(sum(mean_variances)),rtol=1e-12,atol=1e-12)
        calls=run["evaluations"]
        point=(np.array(expected_initial)+np.pi)%(2*np.pi)-np.pi
        for iteration in run["iterations"]:
            incumbent=calls[iteration["incumbent_evaluation"]]
            proposals=[calls[i] for i in iteration["proposal_evaluations"]]
            assert len(proposals)==2*dimension
            np.testing.assert_allclose(incumbent["parameters"],point,rtol=0,atol=1e-12)
            for proposal in proposals:
                expected=point.copy()
                expected[proposal["axis"]]+=proposal["direction"]*iteration["step"]
                expected=(expected+np.pi)%(2*np.pi)-np.pi
                np.testing.assert_allclose(proposal["parameters"],expected,rtol=0,atol=1e-12)
            best=min(proposals,key=lambda item:item["objective_estimate"])
            margin=2*np.hypot(incumbent["estimated_standard_error"],best["estimated_standard_error"])
            accepted=incumbent["objective_estimate"]-best["objective_estimate"]>margin
            assert accepted==iteration["accepted"]
            assert best["index"]==iteration["best_proposal_evaluation"]
            if accepted: point=np.array(best["parameters"])
            np.testing.assert_allclose(iteration["parameters_after"],point,rtol=0,atol=1e-12)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(run["parameters"],point,rtol=0,atol=1e-12)
        diagnostic=run["diagnostic"]
        parameters=run["parameters"]
        if algorithm=="qaoa":
            values=independent_cuts(width,edges)
            optimum=float(values.max())
            assert diagnostic["classical_optimum"]==optimum
            np.testing.assert_array_equal(diagnostic["cut_values"],values)
            state=independent_qaoa_state(width,edges,parameters)
            raw_quality=float(np.abs(state)**2@values)
            quality=raw_quality/optimum
            denominator=optimum
            exact_met=quality>=.80
            np.testing.assert_allclose(diagnostic["exact_expected_cut"],raw_quality,rtol=0,atol=1e-10)
            np.testing.assert_allclose(diagnostic["exact_approximation_ratio"],quality,rtol=0,atol=1e-10)
        else:
            matrix,ground=independent_chain_hamiltonian(width)
            state=independent_chain_state(width,parameters)
            raw_quality=float(np.vdot(state,matrix@state).real)
            quality=(raw_quality-ground)/width
            denominator=width
            exact_met=quality<=.05
            np.testing.assert_allclose(diagnostic["ground_energy"],ground,rtol=0,atol=1e-11)
            np.testing.assert_allclose(diagnostic["exact_energy"],raw_quality,rtol=0,atol=1e-10)
            np.testing.assert_allclose(diagnostic["energy_density_gap"],quality,rtol=0,atol=1e-10)
        actual=opt.quality_scaling_group_circuit(case,parameters,"all_z").remove_final_measurements(inplace=False)
        actual_state=Statevector.from_instruction(actual).data
        np.testing.assert_allclose(abs(np.vdot(state,actual_state)),1.,rtol=0,atol=1e-10)
        assert run["target_met_audit"]==exact_met
        validation=run["validation"]
        group_delta=.05/84
        global_radius=sum((g["outcome_max"]-g["outcome_min"])*np.sqrt(np.log(2/group_delta)/(2*g["shots"]))
                          for g in validation["groups"])/denominator
        local_delta=.05/len(validation["groups"])
        local_radius=sum((g["outcome_max"]-g["outcome_min"])*np.sqrt(np.log(2/local_delta)/(2*g["shots"]))
                         for g in validation["groups"])/denominator
        estimate=-validation["objective_estimate"]/denominator if algorithm=="qaoa" else (validation["objective_estimate"]-ground)/denominator
        bound=validation["quality_bound"]
        np.testing.assert_allclose([bound["normalized_estimate"],bound["simultaneous_radius"],bound["per_run_95_radius"]],
                                   [estimate,global_radius,local_radius],rtol=0,atol=1e-12)
        assert bound["target_status"]==interval_status(algorithm,estimate,global_radius)
        assert bound["precision_supported"]==(global_radius<=.05)
        all_gate_counts.update(weighted)
        run_rows.append({"case":case,"run":run,"quality":quality,"exact_met":exact_met,
                         "estimate":estimate,"global_radius":global_radius,"local_radius":local_radius,
                         "global_status":bound["target_status"],"local_status":interval_status(algorithm,estimate,local_radius),
                         "global_contains":abs(estimate-quality)<=global_radius,
                         "local_contains":abs(estimate-quality)<=local_radius,
                         "weighted_counts":dict(weighted),"total_shots":run["total_shots_including_validation"]})
assert len(run_rows)==72
assert (total_calls,total_groups,total_shots)==(6408,7656,5_859_840)
assert sum(row["case"]["algorithm"]=="qaoa" for row in run_rows)==60
assert sum(row["case"]["algorithm"]=="vqe" for row in run_rows)==12
print({"reconstructed_objective_calls":total_calls,"reconstructed_group_batches":total_groups,
       "modeled_preparations":total_shots,"replayed_sampled_sweeps":72*12,
       "retained_runs":len(run_rows),"all_simultaneous_precision_radii_at_most_0.05":all(row["global_radius"]<=.05 for row in run_rows)})

A bounded-score group of width W with N shots has a Hoeffding radius W\sqrt{\log(2/\delta)/(2N)}. For the per-run 95% interval, failure 0.05 is split among that run’s groups and their radii are summed. For the simultaneous family interval, failure 0.05 is split among all 84 final groups and radii are summed within each objective. VQE energy radii are divided by n; QAOA cut radii are divided by the enumerated classical optimum.

The left panel compares these normalized radii. They depend on the known score ranges and frozen shot budget, not on the observed quality. The right panel counts exact post-run target passes and targets supported by the corresponding final intervals. A wider simultaneous interval can be inconclusive even when the exact toy reference passes. These are counts for one frozen experiment, not a population success-rate estimate or a validation of nominal coverage through repeated studies.

Under the stated independent-sampling model, the family bound covers final fixed-state means conditional on the training history. It excludes adaptive training queries, optimizer convergence, physical faults and coherent synthesis errors.

This notebook runs parameter search using sampled objective estimates on the same four-vertex MaxCut cycle and two-qubit Hamiltonian as the exact-statevector notebook. Independent ideal measurements are simulated by drawing counts from Qiskit statevector probabilities. The unweighted cycle has edges (0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(0,3). We maximize C(z)=\sum_{(u,v)}[z_u\ne z_v], while the search minimizes the sampled negative cut mean. One all-Z measurement scores all edges jointly. QAOA prepares |+\rangle^{\otimes4} with H on every qubit, uses CX–RZ(−\gamma)–CX for each edge, and RX(2\beta) for the mixer. Angles are radians with R_P(\alpha)=e^{-i\alpha P/2}.

VQE minimizes the sampled energy of H=-Z_0-Z_1+\tfrac12X_0X_1 starting from |00\rangle, with R_Y(\theta) on qubit 0 followed by CX(0,1). The Hamiltonian coefficients and energies are dimensionless. A joint all-Z group measures -Z_0-Z_1; a separate all-X group measures \tfrac12X_0X_1. The all-X circuit applies H on both qubits before computational-basis readout. Combining measured Z terms before computing their variance retains their covariance.

The references below are for post-run checks. Neither classical answer is a parameter-search oracle.

Every sweep freshly estimates the incumbent and each negative and positive coordinate proposal. The lowest sampled proposal is accepted only when its apparent decrease exceeds twice the combined estimated standard error. The following check reconstructs every observed mean and sample variance from its measured counts. It then replays the parameter decisions using only measured estimates, standard errors and the prescribed margin. Exact audit fields are excluded from this replay.

All rejected proposals remain in the record and count toward the workload. Re-estimating the incumbent means the displayed sampled trajectory need not be monotone, even when accepted parameter updates appear favorable. The main chapter’s native MyST table is generated independently by the sampled artifact script; this notebook reports its own fresh execution.

def outcome_score(algorithm, group, bits):
    z = int(bits, 2)
    if algorithm == "qaoa":
        return float(sum(((z >> u) & 1) != ((z >> v) & 1) for u, v in edges))
    if group["group"] == "all_z":
        return -(1 - 2*((z >> 0) & 1)) - (1 - 2*((z >> 1) & 1))
    return .5*(1 - 2*((z >> 0) & 1))*(1 - 2*((z >> 1) & 1))


for algorithm in ("qaoa", "vqe"):
    dimension = 2 if algorithm == "qaoa" else 1
    expected_training_calls = 1 + 32*(1 + 2*dimension)
    expected_training_shots = (1 if algorithm == "qaoa" else 2)*(256 + (1 + 2*dimension)*8*(256 + 512 + 1024 + 2048))
    for run in sampled[algorithm]["runs"]:
        assert run["objective_evaluations"] == expected_training_calls
        assert run["iteration_count"] == 32
        assert run["stop_reason"] == "fixed_schedule_exhausted"
        assert run["total_shots"] == expected_training_shots
        calls = run["evaluations"]
        for call in calls + [run["validation"]]:
            means, mean_variances = [], []
            for group in call["groups"]:
                assert sum(group["counts"].values()) == group["shots"]
                mean = sum(count*outcome_score(algorithm, group, bits)
                           for bits, count in group["counts"].items()) / group["shots"]
                variance = sum(count*(outcome_score(algorithm, group, bits) - mean)**2
                               for bits, count in group["counts"].items()) / (group["shots"] - 1)
                np.testing.assert_allclose(mean, group["estimate"], rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
                np.testing.assert_allclose(variance, group["sample_variance"], rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12)
                means.append(mean)
                mean_variances.append(variance/group["shots"])
            signed_mean = -sum(means) if algorithm == "qaoa" else sum(means)
            np.testing.assert_allclose(signed_mean, call["objective_estimate"], rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
            np.testing.assert_allclose(np.sqrt(sum(mean_variances)), call["estimated_standard_error"], rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12)
        point = (np.array(run["initial"]) + np.pi) % (2*np.pi) - np.pi
        for iteration in run["iterations"]:
            incumbent = calls[iteration["incumbent_evaluation"]]
            proposals = [calls[index] for index in iteration["proposal_evaluations"]]
            np.testing.assert_allclose(incumbent["parameters"], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
            best = min(proposals, key=lambda item: item["objective_estimate"])
            margin = 2*np.hypot(incumbent["estimated_standard_error"], best["estimated_standard_error"])
            accepted = incumbent["objective_estimate"] - best["objective_estimate"] > margin
            assert accepted == iteration["accepted"]
            assert best["index"] == iteration["best_proposal_evaluation"]
            if accepted:
                point = np.array(best["parameters"])
            np.testing.assert_allclose(iteration["parameters_after"], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(run["parameters"], point, rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
        assert all(group["rng"]["spawn_key"][0] == 0 for call in calls for group in call["groups"])
        assert all(group["rng"]["spawn_key"][0] == 1 for group in run["validation"]["groups"])
print("Reconstructed all 780 training/validation objective calls from counts and replayed all 192 sampled sweeps.")

This notebook checks one SKW-style quantum-walk search primitive on a four-dimensional hypercube with 16 vertices. The supplied marked vertex is 5 (0101) and the number of walk steps is fixed at four before checking the probability scan. The target is a teaching equality predicate used to construct the circuit. These results do not establish a database-search benchmark, a MaxCut optimizer, or an application speedup.

The circuit contains the state preparation, joint coin/position marking operation, coin reflection, explicit controlled shifts, clean-work uncomputation, and final measurements of all 11 qubits. An independent classical matrix checks the ideal amplitudes. Counts are seeded classical draws from circuit statevector probabilities; a physical device is not executed. Workspace outcomes remain in the distribution and are never filtered.

The method follows Shenvi, Kempe and Whaley 

Shenvi et al., 2003, Quantum random-walk search algorithm, Physical Review A 67, 052307 (2003), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevA.67.052307. Our original circuit construction uses a binary coin and a clean CCX chain. It differs from the standard uncontrolled SKW step by an overall minus sign. This notebook is a bounded numerical implementation check, not a formal proof of the full algorithm.

Use the pinned Python 3.12 environment. The notebook loads the actual worktree source explicitly, or the matching walk optimization.py download placed beside it. The implementation and notebook are MIT; the output below records exact Qiskit, NumPy and Matplotlib versions.

For hypercube dimension d, the position has N=2^d vertices and the coin selects one of d directions. The generator supports d\in\{2,4,8,16\}, so the coin is a binary register of r=\log_2 d qubits. The integer basis index isj=c+2^r x+2^{d+r}w,

where c is the coin direction, x the position and w the clean-work register. For the fixed d=4 case there are two coin, four position and five workspace qubits. H on the six active wires prepares uniform coin and position; workspace starts at zero.

Write |s\rangle=d^{-1/2}\sum_c|c\rangle. One implemented step applies, in circuit order:

R=I-2|s,m\rangle\langle s,m|. H on the coin and X wrappers convert the joint condition into an all-one phase. A clean AND chain computes five flags using five CCX gates, Z marks the final flag, and five reversed CCX gates uncompute the workspace.

\widetilde G=I-2|s\rangle\langle s|. For the two-qubit coin this is H, X wrappers, CZ, undo X, H.

S|c,x\rangle=|c,x\oplus2^c\rangle. Four coin-matched CCX gates flip the selected position wire; X wrappers restore the coin encoding.

The standard SKW coin is G=2|s\rangle\langle s|-I. Its marked-position coin block is -I. Therefore S\widetilde G R is minus the standard SKW step. Overall (-1)^k does not change this uncontrolled search’s probabilities. A controlled reuse would require attention to that relative phase.

The final readout measures every qubit. A position is decoded from bits 2–5, and classical equality with the supplied mark identifies success. Clean-work leakage is checked as an implementation diagnostic; it is not a postselection success probability.

records.content:
The independent reference below uses active-space index x d+c, directly constructs the 64\times64 standard coin blocks and a shift permutation, and multiplies those matrices. It does not call the circuit builders or use their oracle decomposition. The reference and the implemented circuit are compared after accounting for the known overall (-1)^k phase; a separate total-workspace probability checks uncomputation.

The reference is intentionally bounded. Here it is small enough to inspect the full ideal amplitudes. It supplies evidence for this circuit and input, without proving asymptotic query complexity, uniform algorithm correctness, or noisy-device fidelity.

def independent_skw_state(dimension, marked_vertex, steps):
    r = dimension.bit_length() - 1
    if dimension + r > 6:
        raise ValueError("This notebook's independent dense reference is capped at six active qubits.")
    n_positions = 1 << dimension
    size = n_positions * dimension
    grover_coin = 2 / dimension * np.ones((dimension, dimension)) - np.eye(dimension)
    coin_operator = np.zeros((size, size), dtype=complex)
    shift_operator = np.zeros((size, size), dtype=complex)
    for x in range(n_positions):
        block = slice(x * dimension, (x + 1) * dimension)
        coin_operator[block, block] = -np.eye(dimension) if x == marked_vertex else grover_coin
        for c in range(dimension):
            shift_operator[(x ^ (1 << c)) * dimension + c, x * dimension + c] = 1
    standard_step = shift_operator @ coin_operator
    np.testing.assert_allclose(standard_step.conj().T @ standard_step, np.eye(size), rtol=0, atol=1e-14)
    reference = np.ones(size, dtype=complex) / math.sqrt(size)
    for _ in range(steps):
        reference = standard_step @ reference
    return reference

A product of four single-system marginals preserves the local Z0 mean but generally changes the selected joint state, ZZ witnesses and all 16 probabilities. This is a classical diagnostic only. It is no replacement quantum circuit or pruning rule.

The saved raw trace and once-at-output numerical divisor remain visible alongside the full normalized system density. The comparison with actual Clifford+T is made only when that complete prepared stage exists.

def local_marginal(state,q):
    result=np.zeros((2,2),dtype=complex)
    rest=[j for j in range(4) if j!=q]
    for a in range(2):
        for b in range(2):
            for x in range(8):
                offset=sum(((x>>k)&1)<<j for k,j in enumerate(rest))
                result[a,b]+=state[offset|(a<<q),offset|(b<<q)]
    return result
marginals=[local_marginal(rho,q) for q in range(4)]

ct_counts=None
t_wires=Counter()
first_resets=reuse_resets=0
if prepared is not None:
    text=(asset_dir/"clifford-t-trial.qasm").read_text()
    assert not re.search(r"^\s*gate\s",text,re.MULTILINE), "This pinned CT export must contain only explicit standard primitives."
    ct_counts=Counter()
    active=set()
    output_started=False
    for line in text.splitlines():
        line=line.strip()
        measured=re.fullmatch(r"c\[(\d+)\]\s*=\s*measure\s+(?:q\[(\d+)\]|\$(\d+));",line)
        if measured:
            wire=int(measured.group(2) or measured.group(3))
            assert wire in active
            ct_counts["measure"]+=1
            output_started=True
            continue
        gate=re.match(r"^(h|x|y|z|s|sdg|t|tdg|cx|reset|barrier)\s+(.+);$",line)
        if not gate:
            continue
        name,arguments=gate.groups()
        wires=[int(q or physical) for q,physical in re.findall(r"q\[(\d+)\]|\$(\d+)",arguments)]
        ct_counts[name]+=1
        if name=="barrier":
            continue
        assert not output_started, "No quantum work may follow the first final readout."
        if name=="reset":
            assert len(wires)==1
            if wires[0] not in active:

            else:

                t_wires[(name,wires[0])]+=1
    assert dict(ct_counts)==synthesis["clifford_t_counts"]

This notebook requires its completed source-preflight evidence and copied modules; it verifies loaded native records and executes only the source check. In a downloaded directory, place the Python modules, manifest/results/inventory/CSV, QASMs, lock, license and references beside this notebook. Git, a GPU and native synthesis are unnecessary for its source check.

The earlier five-wire defaults, six-wire density hard ceiling and one-million shared materialization guard remain unchanged. The new named APIs require explicit 8/20k/2m limits. Historical ensemble rejection and any actual one-million guard rejection retain their own scope; a post-generation guard check is not an executed legacy synthesis attempt. All originals stay intact and the inventory measures local logical bytes, not public hosting occupancy.

Saved QASM and sequence hashes identify native synthesis; its backend exposes no seed API. Compiler seed7 is fixed. Measured-instrument QASM omits overall phase and is not a controlled-oracle specification. Coherent unitary-segment reuse requires its phase convention and recorded phase. Offline preprocessing/report time, layout certification, decoder throughput and hardware calibration retain separate scope. Full-family physical confidence and any matched co-design improvement remain unimplemented.

if "frozen_before" in manifest:
    assert manifest["frozen_before"]==manifest["frozen_after"]
    assert manifest["whole_family_physical_completed"] is False
    assert manifest["synthesis_seed"] is None and manifest["transpiler_seed"]==7
else:
    assert prepared is None and manifest["full_clifford_t_trial_completed"] is False
    assert manifest["physical_results_completed"] is False
    print("Original failed-attempt seed/revision/frozen metadata were not recorded; no native or hardware result is inferred.")
assert manifest["private_cache_distributed"] is False
caps=manifest["run_caps"]
assert caps["physical_cases"]==caps["prepared_synthesis_stages"]==1 and caps["physical_profiles"]==2
assert caps["density_wires"]==8 and caps["density_matrix_bytes"]==1048576
assert caps["native_rotation_synthesis_attempts_upper_bound"]==23632
assert caps["factory_queries_per_profile"]==caps["surface_code_queries_per_profile"]==24
assert caps["factory_candidates_per_query"]==1000 and caps["factory_candidates_per_profile"]==24000
assert caps["managed_json_qasm_bytes"]==32*1024**2 and caps["private_checkpoint_bytes"]==256*1024**2
assert caps["prepare_seconds"]==1800 and caps["parent_seconds"]==2400
if prepared is not None:
    assert prepared["hardware_execution"] is False and prepared["formal_confidence_certificate"] is False
    assert prepared["joint_system_correlations_preserved"] is True
    assert prepared["unobserved_reset_histories_are_measured_outputs"] is False
    assert synthesis["actual_synthesis_sequences_generated"] is True
    assert synthesis["preserve_full_unitary"] is True and synthesis["transpiler_qubits_initially_zero"] is False
    assert synthesis["formal_interval_certificate"] is False
    assert 0<synthesis["native_rotation_synthesis_attempts"]<=23632
    print("Observed native attempts:",synthesis["native_rotation_synthesis_attempts"])
    print("Actual unique targets:",synthesis["unique_rotation_targets"])
phases=dict(preflight["qasm_export"]["in_memory_global_phase_radians"])
if prepared is not None:
    phases.update(prepared["qasm_export"]["in_memory_global_phase_radians"])
    assert phases["clifford-t-trial.qasm"]==synthesis["compiled_global_phase"]
    assert "limits" not in synthesis
    assert synthesis["compiler_domain"]=="literal-n4-explicit-opt-in-v1"
    assert synthesis["materialization_limits"]==asdict(materialization_limits)
    assert synthesis["native_synthesis_backend"]["qiskit_262_cargo_lock_version"]=="0.2.2"
    assert synthesis["native_synthesis_backend"]["upstream_tag_commit"]=="0e94e5638c42624f4ec358f5eab079942462d2bf"
    legacy_materialization=prepared["legacy_materialization_validation"]
    assert legacy_materialization["legacy_operation_cap"]==1000000
    assert legacy_materialization["actual_operations"]==sum(synthesis["clifford_t_counts"].values())
    assert legacy_materialization["legacy_synthesis_performed"] is False
    assert legacy_materialization["legacy_physical_estimation_performed"] is False
    if legacy_materialization["actual_operations"]>1000000:
        assert legacy_materialization["status"]=="rejected_actual_clifford_t_operations"
        assert legacy_materialization["rejection_reproduced"] is True
    else:
        assert legacy_materialization["status"]=="passed_frozen_operation_guard"
assert set(phases)==set(qasm_hashes) and all(math.isfinite(v) for v in phases.values())
historical_n4=next((record for record in family_records if record["n_system"]==4),None)
if historical_n4 is not None:
    assert historical_n4["density_checker_status"]=="density_width_cap_exceeded"
    assert historical_n4["density_required_wires"]==8 and historical_n4["density_supported_wires"]==6
    assert historical_n4["density_width_rejection_reproduced"] is True
    assert historical_n4["limits"]["validation_branches"]==256
    assert historical_n4["legacy_synthesis_performed"] is False
    assert historical_n4["legacy_physical_estimation_performed"] is False
    assert historical_n4["family_allocation_reallocated"] is False
    if stage_status.get("family",{}).get("status")=="completed":
        assert historical_n4["status"]=="ensemble_branch_cap_exceeded"
        assert historical_n4["rejection_reproduced"] is True and "branch cap" in historical_n4["reason"]
    else:
        print("Current complete family diagnostic status was not recorded; the retained historical status is",historical_n4["status"])
else:
    print("No historical family diagnostic was retained in this failed capsule.")
legacy_bounds=legacy_di.DenseInstrumentLimits(max_qubits=6,source_operations=20000,validation_operations=1000000)
try:
    legacy_di.validate_density_source(source,limits=legacy_bounds)
except ValueError as error:
    assert "width" in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError("The historical six-wire density cap must still reject this source.")
for record in family_records:
    if record["n_system"] in (2,3):
        assert record["regenerated"] is False
        assert record["source_or_synthesis_rerun"] is False
table(pd.DataFrame([{"cap":name.replace("_"," "),"value":value} for name,value in caps.items() if isinstance(value,int) and not isinstance(value,bool)]))
inventory=pd.read_csv(asset_dir/"artifact-inventory.csv")

assert len(inventory)==inventory_record["payload_files"]==manifest["artifact_inventory"]["payload_files"]
assert int(inventory["bytes"].sum())==inventory_record["payload_bytes"]==manifest["artifact_inventory"]["payload_bytes"]
assert inventory_record["originals_preserved"] is True
for row in inventory.to_dict("records"):
    raw=(asset_dir/row["file"]).read_bytes()
    assert len(raw)==row["bytes"] and hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()==row["sha256"], row["file"]
table(inventory.groupby("category",sort=False).agg(files=("file","count"),bytes=("bytes","sum")).reset_index())
print("Managed local payload:",inventory_record["payload_files"],"files;",inventory_record["payload_bytes"],"bytes. Recursive metadata is separate; this is not public hosting occupancy.")
print("Source/correlations, complete readouts, budgets, loaded status records and preserved old domains verified.")

This following resource study fixes the interacting chain at n=2, r=69, Z0 and 15,756 complete trials. Every trial retains all 209 resets, input gates, damping halves and four final readouts. The realized score is +1/−1; all other system/environment records are ignored. There is no algorithm postselection.

This notebook checks the saved source/QASM identities and reruns one bounded, literal four-wire source density check. Actual Clifford+T synthesis and serialized physical reports are loaded from the generated bundle; the large trial population and hardware schedule are unexecuted. The n3/r134 and n4/r211 ensemble-cap rejections and unused family allocations stay explicit. No native estimate, new synthesis, GPU or remote run starts here.

from pathlib import Path
from fractions import Fraction
import hashlib, importlib.metadata, json, math, platform, sys
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython import get_ipython
from IPython.display import display

root=Path.cwd()
local=(root/"lindblad_physical_workload.py").is_file()
if not local and root.name=="notebooks" and (root.parent/"src/openquantum/simulation/lindblad_physical_workload.py").is_file():
    root=root.parent
if not local and (root/"src/openquantum/simulation/lindblad_physical_workload.py").is_file():
    sys.path.insert(0,str(root/"src"))
    from openquantum.simulation import lindblad_physical_workload as lp
    from openquantum.simulation import lindblad_workload as lw
    from openquantum import instrument_resources as ir
    asset_dir=root/"assets/generated/simulation/lindblad-physical"
else:
    sys.path.insert(0,str(root))
    import lindblad_physical_workload as lp
    import lindblad_workload as lw
    import instrument_resources as ir
    asset_dir=root
# Restore image output even if another imported artifact used the Agg backend.
get_ipython().run_line_magic("matplotlib","inline")

manifest=json.loads((asset_dir/"manifest.json").read_text())
assert platform.python_version()==manifest["python"], "Use the recorded locked Python runtime."
results=json.loads((asset_dir/"results.json").read_text())
prepared=results["prepared"]
assert prepared is not None, "The recorded preparation stage must complete before this evidence notebook runs."
profiles=results["physical_profiles"]
assert len(profiles)==2
assert {r["profile"]["physical_error_rate"] for r in profiles}=={1e-3,1e-4}
family=results["family"]
family_records=list(family.values()) if isinstance(family,dict) else family
for name,expected in manifest["artifacts_sha256"].items():
    assert hashlib.sha256((asset_dir/name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()==expected, name
for name,expected in manifest["source_sha256"].items():
    assert hashlib.sha256((asset_dir/name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()==expected, name
for module in (lp,lw,ir):
    path=Path(module.__file__)
    assert hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()==manifest["source_sha256"][path.name], path.name
for name,expected in manifest["packages"].items():
    assert importlib.metadata.version(name)==expected, name
limits=ir.InstrumentLimits(**prepared["limits"])
assert limits.max_qubits==4 and limits.source_operations==20000
assert limits.synthesized_operations==limits.validation_operations==500000

def table(frame):
    display(frame.style.hide(axis="index").format(precision=8,na_rep="—"))
def fraction(record):
    return Fraction(record["numerator"],record["denominator"])
def point(report):
    points=report.get("pareto_points",[])
    return min(points,key=lambda p:(p["peak_physical_qubits"],p["worst_case_runtime_all_attempts_ns"])) if points else None
print("Saved source/package/artifact hashes and the four-wire density limits verified.")

The source keeps H=0.6Z_0Z_1+0.35(X_0+X_1), intended damping rates 0.8/0.5, t=1, +i/+ input and all literal Strang components. The fresh density calculation evaluates the complete source circuit through the existing checker. An independent GKSL matrix exponential supplies the target mean; its dense matrix is a classical reference, never a quantum gate.

The saved routed and actual Clifford+T answers are numerical instrument checks. They do not prove the representation or SDK norm reserves. The normalization trace is not a postselection probability.

task=lw.ChainTask(2)
assert lw.select_steps(task)==69
assert lw.output_contract()["complete_trials_per_case"]==15756
source=lw.build_chain_circuit(2,task.time,task.J,task.hx,task.rates,69,2,"product",observable="Z")
assert source.num_qubits==source.num_clbits==4
assert source.count_ops()["reset"]==209 and source.count_ops()["measure"]==4
fresh=ir.simulate_trial(source,0,{},limits=limits)
reference=lw.reference_density(task)
observable=lw.on_wire(lw.Z,0,2)
exact=float(np.trace(observable@reference).real)
assert abs(fresh["mean"]-prepared["source_instrument_check"]["mean"])<1e-10
assert abs(fresh["mean"]-exact)<=float(lw.uniform_split_bound(task,69))+1e-10
assert abs(fresh["acceptance_probability"]-1)<1e-10
answers=[{"stage":"GKSL reference","Z0":exact},
         {"stage":"Fresh literal source","Z0":fresh["mean"]},
         {"stage":"Saved routed","Z0":prepared["routed_instrument_check"]["mean"]},
         {"stage":"Saved actual Clifford+T","Z0":prepared["clifford_t_instrument_check"]["mean"]}]
table(pd.DataFrame(answers))
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8,3.5))
labels=[r["stage"] for r in answers[1:]]
ax.bar(labels,[max(abs(r["Z0"]-exact),1e-16) for r in answers[1:]],color=["#365e88","#85a79a","#a56737"])
ax.set(ylim=(0,max(abs(r["Z0"]-exact) for r in answers[1:])*1.25),ylabel="Absolute Z0 bias",title="Source and saved ideal instruments versus GKSL")
ax.ticklabel_format(axis="y",style="sci",scilimits=(-3,3))
ax.tick_params(axis="x",rotation=15)
ax.grid(axis="y",alpha=.2)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

The per-output target is 0.05: splitting allowance 0.01, realization allowance 0.01 and statistics 0.03. The uniform source bound refers to exact decimal parameters and ideal exact substeps. Stored binary64 sub-times and damping angles need a separate representation premise. SDK control/routing and guarded actual Ross–Selinger synthesis are further stages.

The requested whole-circuit synthesis allowance is 5\times10^{-5}. The saved actual guarded sum, representation reserve 

10-7 and SDK reserve 

10-7 form a conditional coherent error \eta. Ideal reset/discard contraction gives unconditional Z0 mean change at most 2\eta; this deterministic bias is not multiplied by the trial count. Neither reserve is inferred from density agreement. Exact rational input/H-angle discrepancies have narrower coverage than a full representation certificate.

c=prepared["error_contract"]
representation=prepared["representation_check"]
assert fraction(c["splitting_bias_exact"])==lw.uniform_split_bound(task,69)
assert fraction(c["whole_realization_error_exact"])*2<=Fraction(1,100)
assert c["absolute_Z0_error_upper_proposal"]<=.05
assert c["representation_norm_reserve_scenario"]==c["SDK_control_routing_norm_reserve_scenario"]==1e-7
assert c["reserve_is_inferred_from_density_agreement"] is False
assert c["coherent_error_is_stochastic_failure"] is False
assert c["full_representation_certificate"] is False
budget=[{"stage":"Uniform splitting bound","absolute_Z0_error":c["splitting_bias_upper"],"scope":"exact-substep source"},
        {"stage":"Realization proposal","absolute_Z0_error":c["realization_Z0_bias_upper_proposal"],"scope":"actual numerical synthesis + two conditional reserves"},
        {"stage":"Statistics allowance","absolute_Z0_error":c["statistical_absolute_error"],"scope":"15,756 independent complete scores"}]
table(pd.DataFrame(budget))
table(pd.DataFrame([{"guarded_actual_synthesis_error":c["guarded_actual_synthesis_error"],
                    "representation_norm_reserve":c["representation_norm_reserve_scenario"],
                    "SDK_norm_reserve":c["SDK_control_routing_norm_reserve_scenario"],
                    "exact_H_angle_component_upper":representation["Hamiltonian_angle_coherent_error_component_upper"],
                    "representation_reserve_certified":representation["representation_reserve_is_certified"]}]))
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8,3.5))
bottom=0
for row,color in zip(budget,("#365e88","#a56737","#85a79a")):
    ax.bar(["n2/r69/Z0"],[row["absolute_Z0_error"]],bottom=bottom,label=row["stage"],color=color,width=.45)
    bottom+=row["absolute_Z0_error"]
ax.axhline(.05,color="#555555",linestyle="--",label="Target 0.05")
ax.set(ylabel="Absolute Z0 error",ylim=(0,.058),title="Source, conditional realization and statistics stay separate")
ax.legend(fontsize=8,loc="upper left",bbox_to_anchor=(1,1))
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

All 15,756 trials run the complete schedule. Each has 209 source resets and four readouts, plus 11 additional reserved workspace/bridge initializations in the physical model. The implementation retains the original literal r69 source rather than removing commuting damping halves.

The family statistics allowance remains 0.005, or 1/600 per case. Physical faults and factory readiness each receive 0.0025 for the family, or 1/1200 per case. The n2 slice uses its unchanged shares. n3/r134 and n4/r211 reject in the 256-branch source ensemble and have no physical implementation; their allocations are not reassigned. There is no simultaneous hardware-confidence claim for all three outputs.

w=prepared["complete_workload"]
counts=w["primitive_counts_per_complete_trial"]
assert w["complete_trials"]==w["complete_attempts"]==15756
assert w["algorithm_retry_cap"]==1 and w["postselection"]=="none"
assert w["reset_per_trial"]==counts["reset"]==209
assert w["readout_per_trial"]==counts["measure"]==4
assert w["source_resets_all_trials"]==3293004 and w["source_readouts_all_trials"]==63024
assert w["workspace_startup_initializations_all_trials"]==11*15756
for name,count in counts.items():
    assert w["primitive_counts_all_trials"][name]==count*15756
allocations=prepared["family_allocations"]
assert allocations["unused_cases_reallocated"] is False
assert allocations["family_physical_confidence_implemented"] is False
for n,allocation in allocations["case_allocations"].items():
    assert fraction(allocation["statistical_failure_exact"])==Fraction(1,600)
    assert fraction(allocation["physical_failure_exact"])==Fraction(1,1200)
    assert fraction(allocation["factory_availability_failure_exact"])==Fraction(1,1200)
family_table=[{"systems":r["n_system"],"steps":r["selected_steps"],"complete_trials":r["complete_trials"],
               "status":r["status"],"physical_status":(", ".join(dict.fromkeys(p["status"] for p in profiles)) if r["n_system"]==2 else r.get("physical_status",r["status"]))} for r in family_records]
table(pd.DataFrame(family_table))
groups={"Local Cliffords":sum(counts.get(g,0) for g in ("h","x","y","z","s","sdg")),
        "T / T-dagger":sum(counts.get(g,0) for g in ("t","tdg")),
        "Neighbor CNOT":counts.get("cx",0),"Source resets":counts["reset"],"Readouts":counts["measure"]}
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8,3.7))
ax.bar(groups.keys(),[v*15756 for v in groups.values()],color=["#365e88","#a56737","#85a79a","#876488","#a0aab2"])
ax.set(yscale="log",ylabel="Actual primitive occurrences across all complete trials",title="Calculated Clifford+T population; trials unexecuted")
ax.tick_params(axis="x",rotation=20)
ax.grid(axis="y",alpha=.2)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

The reports keep physical error 

10-3 or 

10-4 and the default controller error 

10-15 per decision. These are alternative physical assumptions for the same complete task. Gates/initialization take 100 ns, readout 500 ns, code cycles 1,000 ns and controller reaction 10,000 ns. Reset/readout, startup, idle exposure, trial dispatch, routing, neighboring transport, injection/correction and complete factory retries are charged. Peak space adds one native factory to 15 reserved logical patches.

The points below are conditional QDK/ledger calculations, not executed hardware schedules. Infeasibility or a query/instruction/time cap remains explicit. Protected parity geometry, tracked frames and factory handoff remain assumptions. The model is separate from the frozen Grover/PSSPC baseline.

rows=[]
for report in profiles:
    p=report["profile"]
    assert p["physical_error_rate"] in (1e-3,1e-4)
    assert p["controller_failure_per_decision"]==1e-15
    best=point(report)
    rows.append({"physical_error":p["physical_error_rate"],"status":report["status"],
                 "distance":best["data_code_distance"] if best else None,
                 "peak_physical_qubits":best["peak_physical_qubits"] if best else None,
                 "all_trial_hours":best["worst_case_runtime_all_attempts_ns"]/3.6e12 if best else None,
                 "Pareto_points":len(report.get("pareto_points",[]))})
table(pd.DataFrame(rows))
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8,3.8))
plotted=False
for report,color in zip(profiles,("#365e88","#a56737")):
    points=report.get("pareto_points",[])
    if points:
        plotted=True
        ax.plot([p["peak_physical_qubits"] for p in points],[p["worst_case_runtime_all_attempts_ns"]/3.6e12 for p in points],
                "o-",color=color,label=f"Physical error {report['profile']['physical_error_rate']:g}")
        for p in points:
            ax.annotate(f"d={p['data_code_distance']}",(p["peak_physical_qubits"],p["worst_case_runtime_all_attempts_ns"]/3.6e12),
                        xytext=(4,3),textcoords="offset points",fontsize=7)
if plotted:
    ax.set(xscale="log",yscale="log")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)
else:
    ax.text(.5,.5,"No computed feasible profile; see explicit statuses",ha="center",va="center",transform=ax.transAxes)
ax.set(xlabel="Peak physical qubits",ylabel="All-trial runtime (hours)",title="Conditional qubit/time frontier for the fixed n2 task")
ax.grid(alpha=.2)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Physical fault components add within the engineering model. Native factory output quality is counted once; the availability of enough accepted factory pipelines has its own 1/1200 case budget. Complete pipeline retries include timing and controller work. A controller contribution is a model term, not a lower bound on actual hardware failure.

For the minimum-space Pareto point in each computed profile, the following checks compare the saved component sum and its physical allocation. The readiness bound is shown separately rather than folded into synthesis or algorithm acceptance.

component_names=("data_workspace_code_exposure","factory_output_handoff_storage","logical_readout_scenario",
                 "logical_initialization_scenario","controller_scenario","factory_output_quality_model")
fault_rows=[]
feasible=[]
for report in profiles:
    best=point(report)
    if best:
        feasible.append((report,best))
        components=best["failure_components_all_attempts"]
        assert math.isclose(sum(components.values()),best["full_physical_failure_model"],rel_tol=1e-10,abs_tol=1e-13)
        assert best["full_physical_failure_model"]<=report["physical_failure_budget"]
        assert best["factory_supply"]["availability_failure_union_bound"]<=report["factory_availability_budget"]
        assert best["reserved_logical_patches"]==15
        fault_rows.append({"physical_error":report["profile"]["physical_error_rate"],
                           "physical_fault_model":best["full_physical_failure_model"],
                           "physical_budget":report["physical_failure_budget"],
                           "readiness_model":best["factory_supply"]["availability_failure_union_bound"],
                           "readiness_budget":report["factory_availability_budget"],
                           "factory_retry_cap":best["factory_supply"]["full_pipeline_retry_cap_per_state"]})
    else:
        fault_rows.append({"physical_error":report["profile"]["physical_error_rate"],"status":report["status"]})
table(pd.DataFrame(fault_rows))
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8,3.7))
if feasible:
    x=np.arange(len(feasible))
    bottom=np.zeros(len(feasible))
    colors=("#365e88","#a0aab2","#85a79a","#876488","#a56737","#bd926e")
    for name,color in zip(component_names,colors):
        values=np.array([p["failure_components_all_attempts"][name] for _,p in feasible])
        ax.bar(x,values,bottom=bottom,label=name.replace("_"," "),color=color,width=.55)
        bottom+=values
    ax.axhline(float(Fraction(1,1200)),color="#555555",linestyle="--",label="Physical case allowance")
    ax.set(xticks=x,xticklabels=[f"p={r['profile']['physical_error_rate']:g}" for r,_ in feasible])
    ax.legend(fontsize=7,loc="upper left",bbox_to_anchor=(1,1))
else:
    ax.text(.5,.5,"No computed components; see explicit statuses",ha="center",va="center",transform=ax.transAxes)
ax.set(ylabel="All-trial additive physical fault model",title="Fault components; readiness has a separate budget")
ax.grid(axis="y",alpha=.2)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

In the checkout use PYTHONPATH=src python scripts/generate_simulation_lindblad_physical.py. This notebook loads the resulting native evidence and performs only a bounded source check. For an independent notebook run, save all copied Python sources, manifest/results/CSV, QASM files, lock, license and references beside this notebook.

The fixed run permits one prepared workload, source 20,000 instructions, synthesized/density validation 500,000, one four-wire density check path, two physical profiles and the declared 256-branch diagnostic rejections. Stage and native-query caps are recorded below; candidates are not silently truncated. A prepared whole-circuit stage may make several native rotation-synthesis attempts; the attempt cap is separate from the stage count. Saved sequence hashes identify unseeded native synthesis. Measured-trial QASM omits overall phase; coherent controlled reuse of unitary segments requires source or phase restoration.

The representation/SDK reserves, factory interface, memory/initialization/readout scenarios and hardware calibration have distinct scopes. Offline preprocessing/report wall time, layout certification and decoder throughput remain outside quantum runtime. There is no formal synthesis, full representation or hardware confidence certificate and no claimed quantum advantage.

assert manifest["frozen_before"]==manifest["frozen_after"]
assert manifest["private_cache_distributed"] is False
assert manifest["whole_family_physical_completed"] is False
assert manifest["synthesis_seed"] is None and manifest["transpiler_seed"]==7
assert prepared["hardware_execution"] is False and prepared["formal_confidence_certificate"] is False

assert prepared["actual_synthesis"]["actual_synthesis_sequences_generated"] is True
assert prepared["actual_synthesis"]["preserve_full_unitary"] is True
assert prepared["actual_synthesis"]["transpiler_qubits_initially_zero"] is False
for record in family_records:
    if record["n_system"] in (3,4):
        assert record["physical_estimation_performed"] is False
        assert record["synthesis_performed"] is False
        assert record["family_allocation_reallocated"] is False
assert prepared["family_allocations"]["family_physical_confidence_implemented"] is False
caps=prepared["run_caps"]

assert caps["factory_queries_per_profile"]==caps["surface_code_queries_per_profile"]==24
assert caps["factory_candidates_per_query"]==1000

BYTE_CAP = 32*1024**2
root = Path.cwd()

else:

def payload_path(name):
    relative = Path(name)
    assert not relative.is_absolute() and ".." not in relative.parts, name
    path = asset_dir / relative
    assert not path.is_symlink(), name
    for parent in path.parents:
        if parent == asset_dir.parent:
            break
        assert not parent.is_symlink(), name
    return path

def file_bytes(name, maximum=BYTE_CAP):
    path = payload_path(name)
    assert path.is_file() and path.stat().st_size <= maximum, name
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", 0))
    with os.fdopen(fd, "rb") as handle:
        before = os.fstat(handle.fileno())
        assert stat.S_ISREG(before.st_mode) and before.st_size <= maximum, name
        data = handle.read(maximum+1)
        after = os.fstat(handle.fileno())
        assert len(data) <= maximum and before.st_size == after.st_size == len(data), name
    assert not path.is_symlink() and path.stat().st_size == len(data), name
    return data

def load_json(name, maximum=BYTE_CAP):
    value = json.loads(file_bytes(name, maximum))
    assert isinstance(value, dict), name
    return value

def canonical_bytes(value):
    return (json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False)+"\n").encode()

def table(rows):
    frame = rows if isinstance(rows, pd.DataFrame) else pd.DataFrame(rows)
    display(frame.style.hide(axis="index").format(lambda x: f"{x:.9g}" if isinstance(x,(float,np.floating)) else str(x), na_rep="—"))

def density(record):
    value = np.array(record["real"], dtype=float) + 1j*np.array(record["imag"], dtype=float)
    assert value.shape == (16,16) and np.isfinite(value).all()
    return value

def trace_norm(value):
    return float(np.linalg.svd(value, compute_uv=False).sum())

For a rotation on physical wire w, the recipe checks that every wire 0,\ldots,w has already received an explicit initialization. It then moves the data from w to 0 with descending adjacent SWAPs, applies the identical bare recovered token word on 0 and reverses the path with ascending SWAPs. Each SWAP has three nearest-neighbor CNOTs, so the block adds exactly 2w SWAPs or 6w CNOTs. If the initialized-path condition fails, it keeps the original word.

The unchanged factory port reaches each data wire through reserved workspace and adjacent transport. Applying a long Clifford+T word at wire w repeatedly pays that route for its T gates. Moving the data for one whole verified word amortizes the added CNOTs over those T occurrences. In the frozen macro ledger, CX costs 11 controller decisions and moving one T left by one wire removes 33, so this block changes the demand by 33w(2-N_T) for its actual T count N_T. Every T at wire 0 still pays its factory, handoff, workspace and feedback costs.

Restoration happens before the next source instruction. Every nonrotation instruction, reset, ignored readout and barrier remains in order, and the final mapping to c0…c7 remains [6,1,2,3,7,4,0,5]. The original complete compiled phase is carried verbatim once. Word-level phases are checked during recovery and are not added again while embedding their bare tokens.

The canonical recipe binds the saved input hashes, all rotation indices and CT ranges, initialized masks, word identities, swap paths, source code and matched-task contract before candidate execution. Structural recipe counts are distinct from actual emitted-candidate counts.

The local Z0 mean alone cannot validate three interacting systems. The following diagnostic forms a classical product of the source’s single-system marginals. That product has the same local Z0 mean but different ZZ witnesses, joint probabilities and full state. It is not a replacement quantum circuit or a pruning rule.

The full source/routed/Clifford+T 8\times8 states and eight-outcome laws remain in the saved checks. The fresh source is compared with those records. No reset histories are mistaken for measured environment outcomes.

def local_marginal(state,q):
    # Independent explicit partial trace in little-endian three-system order.
    result=np.zeros((2,2),dtype=complex)
    rest=[j for j in range(3) if j!=q]
    for a in range(2):
        for b in range(2):
            for x in range(4):
                offset=sum(((x>>k)&1)<<j for k,j in enumerate(rest))
                result[a,b]+=state[offset|(a<<q),offset|(b<<q)]
    return result

The source circuit prepares a Bell purification from all-zero wires and applies an explicit Pauli LCU approximation to an imaginary-time filter. This notebook amplifies the known prepared input by reflecting about all input wires. It keeps the accepted purification’s direction, including a possible global sign, while the thermal-polynomial bias remains unchanged.

The fixed model is H/E_0=0.6Z+0.4X, E_0=k_B=1, Taylor degree 6 and default \beta=1.25/E_0. One system, one reference and two label qubits give four wires. The primary amplitude-amplification identity is due to Brassard et al. (2000 preprint, published 2002); this implementation and its circuit figures are original.

The original one-spin Hamiltonian is
(H_\omega(t)=Z_S/2-\omega Z_E/2+.08 f(t)X_SX_E), with
(f(t)=\exp[-(t-8)^2/8]) on ([0,16]). Both XX parity branches remain.
The main request uses all 17 Gauss–Legendre frequencies on [0,2], 192 fresh-draw
rounds and 256 positive-time midpoint steps per round. The bath is prepared by
an explicit classical bit/X and discarded/reset after each round.

The system starts in excited computational |0>; its ground is |1>. Thermal
mode has beta=1 and bath probability 1/(1+exp(omega)); ground mode uses bath |0>.
Fresh choices give the power of the averaged channel, not an average of

Extract the ZIP beside the notebook; it creates
